2d7d9a59-43ed-5170-a1ad-4e0390ae0f19.name: Italy participates in WWI on the side of Britain, France and Russia
2d7d9a59-43ed-5170-a1ad-4e0390ae0f19.description: Italy participates in World War I on the side of the UK, France and Russia, despite widespread opposition to entering the war. On the Austrian front, Italy suffers a crushing defeat at Caporetto in 1917, but wins in 1918. In Libya, Arab revolt: Italy keeps control only of coastal towns. Casualties are 650,000 military deaths, 950,000 wounded, 600,000 prisoners of war or missing.

2d935d75-db3b-50d0-8bdd-66d8e7d7cb4c.name: Konstantinos Paparrigopoulos wrote *History of the Greek Nation*
2d935d75-db3b-50d0-8bdd-66d8e7d7cb4c.description: Konstantinos Paparrigopoulos writes a five-volume *History of the Greek Nation*, a highly influential historiographical work about the continuity of Greek history since antiquity.

2dcb16d8-35d0-5c6a-9544-44c46c176666.name: Le Pere Goriot, by Balzac
2dcb16d8-35d0-5c6a-9544-44c46c176666.description: *Le Père Goriot* by Honoré de Balzac tells the tragic story of a father’s love for his two daughters.

2e1d1b80-c0e4-5e32-8092-a5a462def94c.name: The Grand Duchy of Tuscany issues the first official ruling in Italy regarding “those who bath in the sea in the open air.”
2e1d1b80-c0e4-5e32-8092-a5a462def94c.description: The Grand Duchy of Tuscany issues the first official ruling in Italy regarding “those who bathe in the sea in the open air”. Around that time, in Viareggio two wooden bathing establishments are built (one for men, the other for women). They are intended for seawater therapy.

2e37adad-cf4d-5f1b-977c-703891b580bd.name: Restoration of the Zaghouan Aqueduct
2e37adad-cf4d-5f1b-977c-703891b580bd.description: Restoration of the Zaghouan Aqueduct, Tunisia’s largest water-service network, allows supply to the capital and its suburbs.

2e3ee4f6-08c8-5b66-8a7c-50a86cc7a813.name: Queen Caroline of Brunswick visits the Regency
2e3ee4f6-08c8-5b66-8a7c-50a86cc7a813.description: Queen Caroline of Brunswick visits the Regency of Tunis as a guest of the Bey. She is hosted at the Palais de la Rose in Manouba.

2e5553b2-10a1-508c-b514-7cea172d3a79.name: The Great Industrial Exposition opens at Treptower Park
2e5553b2-10a1-508c-b514-7cea172d3a79.description: The Great Industrial Exposition opens at Treptower Park, south of central Berlin.

2e5f01d4-308d-5a70-a988-916c466f2e16.name: Ballet and fashion
2e5f01d4-308d-5a70-a988-916c466f2e16.description: Dance (i.e. the waltz and quadrille), street song and cabaret (i.e. the sentimental and parody) and operetta all caught the popular imagination. Popular novels (i.e. those by Dumas, Sue, du Terrail) enjoyed huge success too, due to serialisation. The fashion world was influenced by publications of specialist journals and department stores where different fashions mark each period (i.e. the crinoline, the corset and millinery fashions).

2e8ea8ca-5cb6-5ea9-bac5-61bda65d030d.name: Gheorghe Asachi teaches a class of drawing and history of art at the School for Surveying Engineers
2e8ea8ca-5cb6-5ea9-bac5-61bda65d030d.description: Gheorghe Asachi teaches a class of drawing and history of art at the School for Surveying Engineers (Moldavia).

2ea80ce5-5a5f-504e-ac0a-cd5a99c386fe.name: Abolished old taxes over real estate income
2ea80ce5-5a5f-504e-ac0a-cd5a99c386fe.description: Statesman and jurist José Mouzinho da Silveira (1780–1851) abolishes old taxes over real estate income, privileges and immunities detrimental to the kingdom’s economy. He creates the Tribunal do Tesouro Público for tax collection and Treasury administration. He defines the powers of the Minister of Finance and regulates Customs administration, among other reforms.

2ed2e8f3-1595-51da-af93-13d2534444aa.name: Nikolaos Gyzis professor at the Academy of Munich
2ed2e8f3-1595-51da-af93-13d2534444aa.description: Nikolaos Gyzis, one of Greece’s most important 19th-century painters, becomes professor at the Academy of Fine Arts, Munich.

2f193798-1c99-5489-8dd4-84052637861c.name: First newspaper in Turkish
2f193798-1c99-5489-8dd4-84052637861c.description: October: First private newspaper to be published by Turkish journalists,*Tercüman-ı Ahvâl*, published by Agah Efendi and İbrahim Şinasi.

2f53789c-449c-5aff-b105-7d621c8784c6.name: Bashir II becomes the leader of Lebanon
2f53789c-449c-5aff-b105-7d621c8784c6.description: Bashir Shihab II, helped by the Ottomans and by Ahmad Pasha al-Jazzar (governor of Acre), defeats his rival in the Battle of Simqanieh. Bashir Jumblatt dies in Acre at the order of al-Jazzar. Bashir II represses the Druze rebellion, particularly in and around Beirut. This makes Bashir II the only leader of Mount Lebanon.

2fd33dd1-fbb1-5cd2-b7e5-5b6157398bbc.name: Tunis, a commercial city
2fd33dd1-fbb1-5cd2-b7e5-5b6157398bbc.description: Situated at the confluence of the seas of the Mediterranean, Tunis is seen as a great commercial city that many of her neighbours fear. Food and luxury goods are in abundance and considerable fortunes are created through international trade and the trade-race at sea.

2fe920bf-dc5d-5d7d-b638-e1fda9c0d68c.name: Rudolf Steiner is originator of the Waldorfpädagogik
2fe920bf-dc5d-5d7d-b638-e1fda9c0d68c.description: Rudolf Steiner, originator of the *Waldorfpädagogik*, opens the first Steiner School in Stuttgart (the basis of which is human anthropology).

2febc0a2-81d5-5bfa-a15b-879cf9bb76b4.name: The stuccoes of the Corridor of the palace
2febc0a2-81d5-5bfa-a15b-879cf9bb76b4.description: The stuccoes of the corridor of the Monserrate Palace are inspired by those of Alhambra Palace in Granada. The profusion of columns is considered to recall those in the Hypostyle Hall of the Cordova Mosque.

300f220d-4297-53b3-adc1-2a2065bf96d5.name: Auguste Mariette
300f220d-4297-53b3-adc1-2a2065bf96d5.description: Excavations of the French scholar, archaeologist and Egyptologist Auguste Mariette (1821–81) in Egypt.

30123690-f935-51d6-b829-15c09c5bf051.name: British occupation of Aden
30123690-f935-51d6-b829-15c09c5bf051.description: British control of India is driven by trade. Steamships require fuelling stations. To this purpose Aden is occupied and controlled imperially from India for a century. Most British control of the Middle East is indirect and informal. Aden becomes a Crown Colony, with partial control of the Hinterland.

305af4b9-138d-53db-b228-3c969898136b.name: The first mixed courts
305af4b9-138d-53db-b228-3c969898136b.description: The first mixed courts are introduced to hear civil and criminal cases involving Muslims and non-Muslims.

30605f3f-79c6-5430-aaef-b20e16b57357.name: Conflicts between the Druse and the Maronite
30605f3f-79c6-5430-aaef-b20e16b57357.description: Conflicts between the Druze and the Maronite Christians explode. A Maronite revolt against the feudal class erupts, lasting till 1858.

30ae24d4-5a18-5e5d-bdd9-4066fb746b01.name: Maronite schools and university
30ae24d4-5a18-5e5d-bdd9-4066fb746b01.description: Maronite clergy move their school from Ghazir to Beirut. Granted the title of university by the authorities, which allows it to grant academic degrees, mainly doctoral degrees in philosophy and theology, the school takes the name of Saint Joseph’s University. Faculties and institutes are founded in subsequent years including, in 1883, a Faculty of Medicine.

3106c810-9760-5647-9174-23dc4f668e24.name: Gustav Mahler
3106c810-9760-5647-9174-23dc4f668e24.description: Gustav Mahler (1860–1911) is born in Kalištĕ in Bohemia; he emigrates from there to Vienna in 1875.

310880fe-bed7-5590-a2ee-1899b9475b0c.name: Yussef Sahib Mosque
310880fe-bed7-5590-a2ee-1899b9475b0c.description: The construction of the Yussef Sahib al-Taba‘a Mosque is the last great architectural ensemble overseen by the Husaynid Regency of Tunis. The mosque is the main unit of this integrated complex, known as a *kulliye*, which also includes a mosque and two madrasas (schools), two mausoleums, a *funduq* (inn), hammam (steamroom), *sabil* (public fountain) and a *suq* (market).

31118e72-76e6-5f6d-bb7c-f7cdc8d5a9af.name: Mohammad Husayn Haykal
31118e72-76e6-5f6d-bb7c-f7cdc8d5a9af.description: Muhammad Husayn Haykal publishes the first volume of *Jean-Jacques Rousseau*. He intended the book to create a cultural intermarriage between the East and West and hoped it would lead to a new intellectual revolution by providing an example to the West.

31145d35-9bbf-55f7-8483-3958176f9a5d.name: Tram lines
31145d35-9bbf-55f7-8483-3958176f9a5d.description: By the end of the 19th century tram lines have increased in cities. Madrid has horse-drawn trams from 1871 and Barcelona from 1872 but the first city with an electric tram is Bilbao in 1896, followed by Cartagena.

314b2c2a-cf63-5274-9f16-b31c0bb7d540.name: roadway bridge over the Douro river in Porto is inaugurated
314b2c2a-cf63-5274-9f16-b31c0bb7d540.description: Opening of D. Luís I road bridge over the Douro River in Porto. At the time this iconic bridge held the record for the longest iron arch in the world (180 m.) It was a huge advance for the urban traffic network since it allowed a road connection between Porto and Vila Nova de Gaia over the Douro.

31bc4c58-1c9f-5bf3-8f62-45f6ba7ee077.name: Portuguese Industrial Exhibition in Avenida da Liberdade
31bc4c58-1c9f-5bf3-8f62-45f6ba7ee077.description: Portuguese Industrial Exhibition in Avenida da Liberdade in Lisbon.

31c567e8-f1c2-529b-834c-8ae597966a68.name: Built in an area assigned to the Casa Pia by the city of Lisbon
31c567e8-f1c2-529b-834c-8ae597966a68.description: 18 August: Praça de Touros do Campo Pequeno (Campo Pequeno Bullring) opens its doors with a gala show. Built in an area assigned to the Casa Pia (educational establishment for children in need) by the city of Lisbon in 1889 the bullring was designed by the architect António José Dias da Silva (1848–1912) and inspired by Madrid's bullring.

3242b960-d715-5749-b04f-c685adaa7c00.name: First electric lighting on the terrace of the Citadel of Cascais
3242b960-d715-5749-b04f-c685adaa7c00.description: 28 September: The first electric lighting on the terrace of the Citadel of Cascais to celebrate the 15th birthday of future King Carlos I (ruling from 1889). A ball commemorates the electric lighting premiere. The daily press celebrate the occasion, saying that the electric light turned the entrance and the royal residence balconies into “a clear and luminous day’’.

3248e245-0818-5ff5-8379-a2daea37deac.name: Publication of Washington Irving's *Tales of the Alhambra*
3248e245-0818-5ff5-8379-a2daea37deac.description: Publication of Washington Irving's *Tales of the Alhambra*, a collection of essays, verbal sketches and stories that Irving began to write while he was staying in the Alhambra in Granada. The book is influenced by Romanticism and includes Spanish legends and traditions.

327c456c-baa1-5d41-b110-e3bc35e816ee.name: Construction of Piazza Vittorio Emanuele in Florence
327c456c-baa1-5d41-b110-e3bc35e816ee.description: Construction of Piazza Vittorio Emanuele (today Piazza della Repubblica) in Florence, after clearing the area of the Ancient Market.

329387ce-641e-554a-a8cf-759215a6a0b4.name: Romanticism
329387ce-641e-554a-a8cf-759215a6a0b4.description: As in literature, painting sees a similar confrontation between Neoclassicism (e.g. the work of Ingres) and Romanticism, the latter also influencing sculpture. Academicism endured throughout the 19th century (i.e. Bouguereau, Gérôme and Cabanel).

329d1133-7c2b-50dc-8054-ad67370f584e.name: Brera Picture Gallery
329d1133-7c2b-50dc-8054-ad67370f584e.description: Brera Picture Gallery, originally created by Maria Teresa of Austria in 1776, becomes an independent museum.

32a08e9a-89f7-50be-89ab-945103f59949.name: The start of the construction of the telephone network in Vienna
32a08e9a-89f7-50be-89ab-945103f59949.description: Construction of the telephone network in Vienna.

32d00314-464d-53f9-994a-a20172127189.name: Workforce in the German Empire
32d00314-464d-53f9-994a-a20172127189.description: One in every ten members of the workforce in the German Empire is foreign (many of them prisoners of war).

32f946ec-2f50-5de0-b6f6-28fcc0e8facb.name: Armistice between Austro-Hungary and the Entente Powers
32f946ec-2f50-5de0-b6f6-28fcc0e8facb.description: Armistice between Austro-Hungary and the Entente Powers (France, Russia and the United Kingdom).

32fcaa4e-3de5-5d1e-bf7d-62fe60a7c94b.name: The Treaty of Sevres
32fcaa4e-3de5-5d1e-bf7d-62fe60a7c94b.description: The Treaty of Sèvres is ratified after the victory of the Balkan Wars and the end of World War I. Consequently, Greece gains administration of the area of Smyrna.

3374a7bb-9d39-587e-aeb9-774f13809a60.name: Repeated skirmishes between British and Qawasimi vessels
3374a7bb-9d39-587e-aeb9-774f13809a60.description: Repeated skirmishes between British and Qawasim vessels are labelled “piracy” by the former and taken as justification to plot the final destruction of the Qawasim by the latter. The British launch naval attacks against the Qawasim strongholds at Ras al-Khaimah along the Gulf and on the Persian littoral. However, the Qawasim succeed in rebuilding their fleet and positions to resume their defensive trade-war against the British and their Omani allies.

3378cc3b-db0b-52cc-b6c8-5e516aa5a673.name: Redesigning and rebuilding of London and other British cities
3378cc3b-db0b-52cc-b6c8-5e516aa5a673.description: This half century is a period of great rebuilding and redesign in London and other British cities – of churches, public buildings, and housing with slum clearance. The building boom extends to the cities of the British Empire and especially in India. British architects study Islamic architecture and its influence can be seen in many British buildings. British architects also practise in the major Levantine commercial cities, such as the Crimean Memorial Church in Constantinople (G. E. Street) and St Mark’s Church in Alexandria (J. W. Wild).

33827288-2833-5c27-9582-d5e2a6e41232.name: The financial success of the Stockton and Darlington Railway
33827288-2833-5c27-9582-d5e2a6e41232.description: The financial success of the Stockton and Darlington Railway encourages large-scale investment in railways, leading to massive growth in the network. The many passengers are entertained on their journeys with inexpensive books, such as John Murray’s “Reading for the Rail” series.

3393f595-1666-5bec-bb2a-945d78797d18.name: Beirut Tram
3393f595-1666-5bec-bb2a-945d78797d18.description: During this period the Beirut Tram covers 12 km around Beirut’s centre. It runs until 1910.

339e2525-411f-53ff-91c0-1195d060b998.name: Werner von Siemens invents dynamo
339e2525-411f-53ff-91c0-1195d060b998.description: Werner von Siemens invents the dynamo.

33a9f859-947f-593d-9053-96436af683d0.name: Book on Islam and science
33a9f859-947f-593d-9053-96436af683d0.description: Namık Kemal writes *Renan Müdafanamesi* (Critique of Renan), a book on Islam and science.

33d1073a-c0cd-567b-a9e8-7aaae1de3e6a.name: Crimean War
33d1073a-c0cd-567b-a9e8-7aaae1de3e6a.description: War between Russia and the Ottoman Empire and its allies France, UK and Piedmont-Savoy. The Crimean War is a consequence of rivalry over the Eastern Question and France’s support of Catholic claims and Russia’s support of Orthodox claims to control the holy sites in Jerusalem. Russia seeks to exploit Ottoman political weakness to gain diplomatic rights for Orthodox subjects of the Empire. Peace established by the Treaty of Paris (1856).

33e12f92-0779-54f7-95bc-643013b956dc.name: The Saint Louis Museum in Carthage
33e12f92-0779-54f7-95bc-643013b956dc.description: The Saint Louis Museum in Carthage is founded in the former seminary of the White Fathers.

3400d43e-48c5-5561-bc5a-8e375c2234d3.name: Beginning of the excavations at Olympia
3400d43e-48c5-5561-bc5a-8e375c2234d3.description: Excavations begin at Olympia under the German archaeologist Ernst Curtius; they continue under German leadership until World War II.

34059680-933a-5a55-9c34-66d43175c219.name: Giuseppe Pellizza da Volpedo paints The fourth Estate
34059680-933a-5a55-9c34-66d43175c219.description: Giuseppe Pellizza da Volpedo paints *The Fourth Estate*, showing workers on strike. The painting will become an icon of the workers’ movement.

34352b64-976c-536f-b35f-5a07f4cceca3.name: First Restoration
34352b64-976c-536f-b35f-5a07f4cceca3.description: First Restoration: the return of the monarchy, referred to as the Bourbon Restoration. Louis XVIII (brother of Louis XVI) facilitated this by accepting a return to the monarchy by means of the Charter of 1814. This Charter combined the more moderate ideas of the Revolution with certain monarchist traditions.

3457ff8f-8815-5674-a90e-0d91d3f17c85.name: New districts
3457ff8f-8815-5674-a90e-0d91d3f17c85.description: Following development of the Port of La Goulette, new districts relating to trade and industrial activities are born. The neighbourhood is given the name of “Little Sicily”, which is suggestive of its role as host to a poor immigrant population mainly from southern Italy.

3459cc92-9d55-5749-b0a8-c76023b06d8d.name: Establishment of the National Roman Museum
3459cc92-9d55-5749-b0a8-c76023b06d8d.description: Establishment of the National Roman Museum, in the stunning structure of the Terme di Diocleziano (Baths of Diocletian) in Rome.

34862ab6-f257-5c9d-8c63-f9c5480fc6d4.name: Opening of the Suez Canal
34862ab6-f257-5c9d-8c63-f9c5480fc6d4.description: Built largely with French expertise and capital, the Suez Canal shortens the journey to India. The British government secures a major financial interest in the Canal in 1876, and its security becomes a major British interest for the following century.

34b05ed8-7b3b-57c5-b08b-b87e6eb4a7f6.name: Emperor Pedro I of Brazil turned Pedro IV of Portugal gave up the throne to his daughter
34b05ed8-7b3b-57c5-b08b-b87e6eb4a7f6.description: With the death of his father, Emperor Pedro I of Brazil becomes Pedro IV of Portugal but gives up the throne to his daughter, future Queen Maria II. The proclamation of a moderate Constitutional Charter does not stop the absolutist movement led by his brother, Prince Miguel (1802–66), who disregards the rights of his niece Princess Maria and Pedro’s decision.

34fcab2b-dc2f-544c-b0e0-dc856d20ac60.name: Aqaba became the new base for Faysal’s army
34fcab2b-dc2f-544c-b0e0-dc856d20ac60.description: In June 1917 the coastal city of Aqaba in Jordan becomes the new base for Faisal’s army, renamed the “Arab Northern Army”. Attacks on the Hijaz Railway continue, extending now as far north as southern Jordan. T. E. Lawrence, “Lawrence of Arabia” himself led reconnaissance parties into Syria and made contact with Arab nationalists in Damascus. The spectacular victory of the Egyptian Expeditionary Force (EEF) at the Third Battle of Gaza (Beersheba) in October 1917, and the subsequent British advance into the Jordan Valley, gave renewed impetus to Faisal’s “railway war” further east. Meanwhile, Amir Faisal, with Lawrence as his adviser, had captured the seaport of Wejh (al-Wagh) on the Red Sea, 150 km north of Yanbu. From there, Faisal’s men spent most of 1917 attacking the Hijaz Railway. Small raiding parties blew up sections of track, destroyed bridges, water towers and even some weakly defended railway stations. The British, planning to invade Palestine, were keen for the Arab rebels to keep the 12,000 Ottoman troops tied down in Medina (Madinah).

35549209-8dfd-5cd7-a86c-f7ff3cf1ef97.name: First government yearbook
35549209-8dfd-5cd7-a86c-f7ff3cf1ef97.description: Publication of the first government yearbook (*salnâme*).

35d1e7c7-dfc8-5a29-8530-3482fa89ccb9.name: Construction of Zubara Fort
35d1e7c7-dfc8-5a29-8530-3482fa89ccb9.description: Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim builds the famous Al Zubarah Fort, in the town of Al Zubarah to protect the northern border.

35e21767-65e7-5114-8acf-969fbb4e0655.name: Portugaliae Monumenta Historica
35e21767-65e7-5114-8acf-969fbb4e0655.description: The *Portugaliae Monumenta Historica* is published. Acknowledged as a historian, Alexandre Herculano is commissioned by Academia das Ciências de Lisboa to compile this collection of old documents that are at risk of disappearing and being dispersed throughout convent archives. He undertook this task in 1853–54.

36273b6e-d387-5a31-b965-0f3ccf0760db.name: Economic increase
36273b6e-d387-5a31-b965-0f3ccf0760db.description: Due to Spain's neutrality in World War I, the economy witnesses increased production and industrial growth. The end of the war produces the beginning of a crisis that causes the end of the monarchy in 1931.

36304388-14c3-51af-8f83-5df47c959257.name: Guilhermina Suggia
36304388-14c3-51af-8f83-5df47c959257.description: The birth of Guilhermina Suggia (d. 1950). This great Portuguese cellist was a pupil of Pablo Casals, with whom she lived for some years. The two were considered the world’s greatest cellists. She played as a soloist with prestigious orchestras. She devoted the last years of her life to teaching but continued to give concerts.

3664b41c-c825-56ea-9c15-a6bb8f81a17c.name: Lendas e  Narrativas
3664b41c-c825-56ea-9c15-a6bb8f81a17c.description: *Lendas e Narrativas* published by Alexandre Herculano (1810–77), a collection of historical short stories set in the context of medieval times and the “Reconquista” process, the Iberian Christian military movement to recover Muslim-occupied territories (10th–15th centuries).

368b9b30-fe58-57b6-ac37-4eb8ad940bfd.name: Isabel II becomes Queen of Spain
368b9b30-fe58-57b6-ac37-4eb8ad940bfd.description: Isabel II becomes Queen of Spain. The Salic Law forbidding women to reign had been abolished in 1830 because Fernando VII's only heirs were female. His brother, Carlos de Borbón, asserts his claim to the throne against his niece (first Carlist War, 1836–39); two further Carlist wars will follow (1846–49, 1872–76).

36ce88f5-732d-54e9-90f3-f50205298555.name: Immigration of the Ruhrpolen
36ce88f5-732d-54e9-90f3-f50205298555.description: The so-called Ruhrpolen migrate to the Ruhr, where many work in coal mining.

36ded29a-588b-5ab2-80e0-00612244d20b.name: Jaroslav Hasek published his parody on the Austrian army
36ded29a-588b-5ab2-80e0-00612244d20b.description: Jaroslav Hašek (1883–1923) publishes his parody on the Austrian army, *The Good Soldier Švejk*.

36edebe3-2697-541c-95fc-38fa5fc6b07d.name: Plan for the modernisation of general education
36edebe3-2697-541c-95fc-38fa5fc6b07d.description: February: A plan for the modernisation of general education is approved.

36fba812-a5fb-5968-aa42-cb52768a1958.name: Hajj Sharif (Pilgrimage) caravans to Mecca
36fba812-a5fb-5968-aa42-cb52768a1958.description: The region enjoyed relative stability due to being the route of the *hajj sharif* (pilgrimage) caravans to Mecca. Sultans and governors took great care of the caravans. *Khan*s, water installations and fortifications were built and maintained along the route and military patrols were formed to protect it.

3718112b-c347-5e00-ac94-928f9f270ecd.name: Law 1176/1919 abolishes marital authorization
3718112b-c347-5e00-ac94-928f9f270ecd.description: Law 1176/1919 abolishes “marital authorisation” and allows women to practise most professions and to take up public employment. But some limitations on women working persist: they are still not allowed to become magistrates, diplomats and police officers or reach the highest grades in the civil service.

37bf8829-e6ef-54b3-bfd7-6c5dda09e2c6.name: Military Coup
37bf8829-e6ef-54b3-bfd7-6c5dda09e2c6.description: A military coup brings about restitution of the Karađorđević Dynasty.

380a001f-0a63-518c-bde9-a0f772b24d79.name: First French woman graduates
380a001f-0a63-518c-bde9-a0f772b24d79.description: The first French Doctorate in literature, Docteur en lettres, is received by a woman.

38203d18-41bd-59f7-a7a5-ae0a56ee450f.name: Grigor Prlichev epic poem The Serdar
38203d18-41bd-59f7-a7a5-ae0a56ee450f.description: Grigor Prlichev's epic poem "The Serdar", written in Greek, wins first prize at the annual poetry competition held in Athens. Prlichev (1830–93) was born in Ohrid. This prolific Macedonian poet and translator was a dedicated advocate of introducing the native spoken language in Macedonian schools. He was referred to as a second Homer, having translated the "Iliad" into the Macedonian language.

382e923b-1910-5e0f-ba53-3972d96b8af6.name: Bashir II and Bashir Jumblatt
382e923b-1910-5e0f-ba53-3972d96b8af6.description: Bashir Shihab II, who was elected as amir in 1788 under Ottoman suzerainty, is overthrown when he backs Acre, and flees to Egypt, later to return and form an army. Bashir Jumblatt, the Druze leader, gathers the Druze factions and declares a rebellion that leads to massacres and battles with the Maronites who support Bashir Shihab.

383d1653-79ab-5139-9743-17029b0cafd9.name: Catholic Emancipation
383d1653-79ab-5139-9743-17029b0cafd9.description: Irish lawyer Daniel O’Connell leads the campaign for concession of Catholic Emancipation, which will allow Roman Catholics to sit in the UK Parliament. The campaign is successful, helped along by the death of George III, but O’Connell’s long-term goal is to repeal Ireland’s Act of Union with Great Britain.

388aea07-bde6-5036-8e0e-f684f0ad4ac6.name: Serbo-Turkish War in Bosnia and Herzegovina
388aea07-bde6-5036-8e0e-f684f0ad4ac6.description: During the 1875 Bosnia-Herzegovina rebellion against Ottoman authority, the principalities of Serbia and Montenegro provide the insurgents with moral, material and military support, which leads to the first Serbo-Turkish War in 1876. Having been a long time in preparation, the rebellion is widespread and raises questions not only about Serbia but also about the East, thus becoming an event of European importance. Its outcome is the convocation of the Berlin Congress (1878), at which both Serbia and Montenegro gain independence, and Austria-Hungary takes over Bosnia-Herzegovina.

390c4a45-9a70-569e-b23c-7391ae4f36f9.name: The first electric tramway is introduced in Bucharest
390c4a45-9a70-569e-b23c-7391ae4f36f9.description: 9 December: the first electric tramway is introduced in Bucharest.

391e794a-87d2-5483-baa5-bd477e8e9f79.name: Reforms of Khayr al-Din
391e794a-87d2-5483-baa5-bd477e8e9f79.description: The regency of Khayr al-Din, the Grand Vizier reformer, who reorganises institutions and the economy. His major cultural works are the creation of Sadiki College and major reform of the Zaytuna Mosque.

393b8cfb-9942-518d-8662-b4c0306464c2.name: Al Qawasim confederation migrates to the Arab Gulf coast
393b8cfb-9942-518d-8662-b4c0306464c2.description: In the early 1700s, the (Al-Qasimi) Qawasim confederation migrates to the coast of the Arab Gulf from the Persian littoral. Here, they establish their main base in Julfar (later Ras al-Khaimah), soon extending their sway all along the lower Gulf, across areas of the east coast and towns on the Persian littoral.

39732a75-8e16-551b-8a7e-558214355925.name: Education during Khedive Ismail era
39732a75-8e16-551b-8a7e-558214355925.description: Education attracts renewed interest during Isma‘il Pasha’s era. His government establishes schools and reviews students’ expenses, including their living expenses, which sees the restoration of the *Diwan* (or ministry) of Schools that Sa‘id had annulled. Now as the education budget increased, gradually, the government also returned to dispatching missions to Europe, mostly to France. A number of primary schools were established across the country: from Alexandria in the north to Minya in the south.

397d1413-dc6e-51b9-b8ea-8b8aee40f1f3.name: Daguerreotypes started to be used in Portugal two years after its invention in France
397d1413-dc6e-51b9-b8ea-8b8aee40f1f3.description: Daguerreotype starts to be used in Portugal two years after its invention in France and is mostly used in commercial portrait lithographs. The oldest ones still existing in Portugal reproduce the Palace (Paços) of Coimbra University in 1842. The University is at the time the major centre for the dissemination of scientific knowledge.

399a756a-6198-592a-a5ba-a5d9f18294d0.name: School of Veterinary Medicine
399a756a-6198-592a-a5ba-a5d9f18294d0.description: A School of Veterinary Medicine emerges in Rashid in 1827, which then transfers to a building beside the School of Medicine at Abu Za‘bal in 1831. Here the veterinary hospital is able to accommodate up to 110 horses and includes a Pharmacy, a Hall of Anatomy and areas for student and staff subsistence.

39bfee98-6c73-5f47-8649-2fb78473366d.name: Slave trade prohibited in South of Equator possessions
39bfee98-6c73-5f47-8649-2fb78473366d.description: The slave trade is prohibited in possessions south of the Equator by a law introduced by Marquis of Sá da Bandeira (1795–1876) for philanthropic and economic reasons. The loss of Brazil, and British pressure, persuades the rulers to endorse abolition to retain in Africa the African labour needed to develop the colonies there. In 1869, King Louis I (1838–89) decrees abolition.

39f11325-f62b-5ea0-a5aa-f48c5105f2c6.name: Germany becomes the biggest industrial nation
39f11325-f62b-5ea0-a5aa-f48c5105f2c6.description: In 1914 Germany becomes the biggest industrial nation within Europe as a result of munitions production before and during World War I.

39f71781-4aca-5f87-b539-b814b2d2a64c.name: Mahmud II leaves Topkapı Palace to live in Beşiktaş Palace
39f71781-4aca-5f87-b539-b814b2d2a64c.description: Mahmud II leaves Topkapı Palace to live in Beşiktaş Palace.

3a266b6a-bbc8-516e-9e1b-80a3c5cd4fd7.name: Dawlat Abyad
3a266b6a-bbc8-516e-9e1b-80a3c5cd4fd7.description: Mrs Dawlat Abyad writes a play to address the various problems experienced by Egyptian women in the early 20th century.

3a677eef-1dda-5449-99cf-0a0d8962f78c.name: The new building of the Viennese Stock Market
3a677eef-1dda-5449-99cf-0a0d8962f78c.description: The Viennese Stock Market is completed to a design by Theophil Hansen.

3a87bb9e-61fa-5226-a29c-2e011ae79146.name: The Welsh poet and writer Dylan Marlais Thomas
3a87bb9e-61fa-5226-a29c-2e011ae79146.description: The Welsh poet and writer Dylan Marlais Thomas is born in Swansea on 27 October 1914. His best known works include the poem “Do not go gentle into that good night” (1951) and the play for voices *Under Milk Wood* (written 1951, first broadcast 1954). In later life, Thomas encouraged his reputation as a “roistering, drunken and doomed poet”; dying prematurely in New York in 1953.

3a97e768-fdfd-5678-82f8-c2c62b2e9f3f.name: The Peace (or Treaty) of Bucharest
3a97e768-fdfd-5678-82f8-c2c62b2e9f3f.description: The Peace (or Treaty) of Bucharest between Romania and Austria.

3b15701c-82c0-5e6d-a2dc-4e153c74aaec.name: The first car in Portugal
3b15701c-82c0-5e6d-a2dc-4e153c74aaec.description: The first car in Portugal, a Panhard et Levassor, is personally imported from Paris by the fourth Count of Avilez. The Lisbon Customs did not know how to tax this awkward item. Was it a farm machine or a locomotive? They chose the second option. Count Jorge Avilez drove from Lisbon to his farm in Santiago do Cacém at 15 km an hour.

3b1d66c5-6b17-5548-b802-869c30f0f68b.name: Foundation of the Museo Nacional de Artes Decorativas
3b1d66c5-6b17-5548-b802-869c30f0f68b.description: Foundation of the Museo Nacional de Artes Decorativas, an important step in the progress of applied arts and design, especially because its main objective is the education of workers, students and the public in the styles, decoration and other aspects of the applied arts.

3b2092d1-ff0b-549c-920b-b9681c7941d3.name: Railway Station of Rossio
3b2092d1-ff0b-549c-920b-b9681c7941d3.description: The railway station of Rossio (Lisbon) designed by the Portuguese architect José Luís Monteiro, begun in 1886 and inaugurated on 23 November of 1890. Located in the historical centre, the Rossio station follows the neo-Manueline architectural style and is an important building of the 19th-century late Romantic style.

3b4b8047-de12-59be-83f4-8d9aa53d7375.name: Inauguration of the first railway of Romania
3b4b8047-de12-59be-83f4-8d9aa53d7375.description: 20 August: inauguration of the first railway of Romania, linking Baziaș to Oravița (in Banat). Used at first to transport coal, it was opened for passenger transportation in 1856. In the United Principalities, the first railway line, built by the British company J.T. Barkley and J. Staniforth, was inaugurated 31 October 1869.

3b5c2397-2fc8-5cf3-9fef-8fb260ae04db.name: Battle of Jena and Auerstedt
3b5c2397-2fc8-5cf3-9fef-8fb260ae04db.description: The twin battles of Jena and Auerstedt are fought – in the midst of the collapse of the Prussian State and abolition of the Holy Roman Empire by Kaiser Franz II – under pressure from Napoleon Bonaparte.

3b805b70-59d9-5dd2-aaf9-74a887611630.name: The National School of Architecture is founded
3b805b70-59d9-5dd2-aaf9-74a887611630.description: The National School of Architecture is founded as a section of the School of Fine Arts in Bucharest. It becomes an independent institution in 1904, under the name the Superior School of Architecture.

3b9bbd62-4250-5e45-99db-e4e400e41e9d.name: The Pietroasa Treasure is displayed at the International Exposition in Paris
3b9bbd62-4250-5e45-99db-e4e400e41e9d.description: The Pietroasa Treasure is displayed at the International Exposition in Paris.

3ba99d7a-2491-544d-813a-2d0e0b87c1ed.name: Establishment of train transportation
3ba99d7a-2491-544d-813a-2d0e0b87c1ed.description: The railway line from the Thesion district in central Athens to the Port of Piraeus opens.

3bab940c-6acd-50ce-afc2-2e2a67e97696.name: Corporation Krupp
3bab940c-6acd-50ce-afc2-2e2a67e97696.description: The Krupp Corporation is the largest industrial concern in Europe.

3c0317ac-c84e-5dfd-8ce0-5b2d23bee52b.name: Telephone
3c0317ac-c84e-5dfd-8ce0-5b2d23bee52b.description: Creation of the telephone network in France.

3c1e33d0-32bc-5e27-aa62-9cb6b0525749.name: Santa Apolónia Central Railway Station of Lisbon
3c1e33d0-32bc-5e27-aa62-9cb6b0525749.description: 1 May: Santa Apolónia Central Railway Station of Lisbon, connecting to the East and North Railways, is inaugurated. It is sited in the north bank of the Tagus River, close to Praça do Comércio in Lisbon. It is an example of 19th-century iron buildings.

3c297ef9-a733-5b96-8bf5-696115f2c95e.name: Anglo Persian Oil Company in Qatar
3c297ef9-a733-5b96-8bf5-696115f2c95e.description: Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim grants the Anglo-Persian Oil Company a two-year exploration licence in Qatar.

3c2b01f4-d0a8-5456-8b65-bbf9ca59d48f.name: Book Dacia before the Romans
3c2b01f4-d0a8-5456-8b65-bbf9ca59d48f.description: Grigore Tocilescu’s book *Dacia before the Romans* is awarded the grand prize of the Academic Society, for the best work on the history of Dacia before the Roman conquest.

3c2bc486-c2d9-5dfe-a9b7-b57f82d9cd6d.name: When the war brakes out, the State takes a leading role in organizing industrial production
3c2bc486-c2d9-5dfe-a9b7-b57f82d9cd6d.description: When the war breaks out, the state takes a leading role in organising industrial production. Dramatic growth of steel, mechanic, chemical and textile productions. Workers in industries of strategic value are submitted to military discipline.

3c48095d-a308-571c-b67f-488d4382e2c0.name: The Neo-Manueline Palace of Bussaco
3c48095d-a308-571c-b67f-488d4382e2c0.description: The neo-Manueline Palace of Bussaco, modelled on the Manueline Belém Tower of Lisbon is commissioned by King Carlos I as a royal retreat. It combines the architectural fashion of castle romanticism (German *Burgenromantik*) with the neo-Manueline gothic style that evokes the Portuguese Discoveries.

3c900370-e13a-5487-878c-06a0d1138786.name: Dukhan, Qatar, Oil Well No. 1
3c900370-e13a-5487-878c-06a0d1138786.description: Dukhan, Qatar, Oil Well No. 1 completed at a depth of 1,733 m, producing around 4,480 barrels of oil per day.

3c91edce-1d52-54ad-82bd-d17232131431.name: Municipal organization for Istanbul
3c91edce-1d52-54ad-82bd-d17232131431.description: The Tanzimat Council appoints a City Ordering Commission (Intizam-ı Şehir Heyeti), comprising Ottoman and foreign residents, charged with developing new regulation to transform the structure of Instanbul into a municipal government. It recommends establishment of a commission to enforce urban regulations and improve the city's physical make-up, financed through a separate tax structure.

3cb9e1c2-bead-5be1-959b-a64de26790ce.name: Romanticism
3cb9e1c2-bead-5be1-959b-a64de26790ce.description: The painting by Caspar David Friedrich, *Der Wanderer über dem Nebelmeer* (1818), exemplifies Romanticism in art at this time.

3d0df806-1a6b-53cb-918d-5a3579339d73.name: The first Railway Station in Macedonia
3d0df806-1a6b-53cb-918d-5a3579339d73.description: Construction of the first railway station in Macedonia in Skopje.

3d0f8752-a96c-5c13-a9bf-51021b32acdc.name: The heir apparent of Austria Franz Ferdinand gets killed in Sarajevo by a member of the Serbian intelligence service
3d0f8752-a96c-5c13-a9bf-51021b32acdc.description: The heir apparent of Austria, Franz Ferdinand, is murdered in Sarajevo by a member of the Serbian intelligence service known as the “Black Hand”. As a consequence, the Austrian government issues an ultimatum to Serbia; Germany declares war on the Russian Empire and on France; and Great Britain declares war on the German Empire.

3d529979-11a8-5eb2-a312-6eb8562c4ae7.name: Chemical industry takes off
3d529979-11a8-5eb2-a312-6eb8562c4ae7.description: The chemical industry takes off. The production of fertilisers grows from 85,700 tons in 1894 to 1 million tons in 1913.

3d6aed71-977a-534c-8fb3-93b2a89a19b4.name: Arts
3d6aed71-977a-534c-8fb3-93b2a89a19b4.description: The arts experience rapid growth with the appearance of new techniques and the emergence of photography and cinema. The female sculptor Camille Claudel was part of this artistic boom. Cultural exchanges with other countries, for example at the International Exhibitions, were extremely fruitful.

3e12f5fd-ba5d-52e4-80bb-44e6a023c956.name: Assasination of the first Governor of Greece
3e12f5fd-ba5d-52e4-80bb-44e6a023c956.description: The First Governor of Greece, Conte Ioannis Kapodistrias, is assassinated.

3e3f4c96-d60d-5a22-a742-4672c2907cea.name: Foundation of the Polytechnic or military school of Bardo
3e3f4c96-d60d-5a22-a742-4672c2907cea.description: Foundation of the Polytechnic or military school of Bardo, responsible for the education of executives of the army and public administration. The School provides education in the art of military strategy, scientific disciplines, foreign languages, literature and religion.

3e41a85d-1cbc-56c2-ae4c-0d6c05f95226.name: Ballet Giselle, by A. Adam
3e41a85d-1cbc-56c2-ae4c-0d6c05f95226.description: The leading roles in *Giselle*, a ballet by Adolphe Adam are played by Carlotta Grisi and Lucien Petipa.

3e450688-88c2-56bb-bfd7-280b207b6d36.name: The German National Assembly meets in Frankfurt
3e450688-88c2-56bb-bfd7-280b207b6d36.description: The German National Assembly meets in Frankfurt.

3e83e3b0-2397-5f16-9d37-897e194c06f4.name: Royal palace (todays Parliament) erected by Friedrich von Gaertner
3e83e3b0-2397-5f16-9d37-897e194c06f4.description: The Royal Palace (today’s Parliament) is erected under the auspices of the director of the Munich Academy of Arts and official architect of the Bavarian court, Friedrich von Gaertner.

3e90d4ec-6cb6-569c-ab8d-01d564d00186.name: Fatma Âliye
3e90d4ec-6cb6-569c-ab8d-01d564d00186.description: Fatma Âliye (1862–1939), female novelist and publisher, publishes *Muhâdarât* (Reminiscence). Her feminist attitude was apparent in her rejection of marriage for economic reasons, believing in the need for women to join the workforce.

3eb7a9b3-273d-5c01-bed5-6041862fc40b.name: Play arouses patriotic sentiments
3eb7a9b3-273d-5c01-bed5-6041862fc40b.description: 1 April: Namık Kemal’s play *Vatan Yahud Silistre* arouses patriotic sentiments in İstanbul.

3f12468c-8073-5acb-80e3-22b455ef5c98.name: Promulgation of the law for the founding of the National Bank of Romania.
3f12468c-8073-5acb-80e3-22b455ef5c98.description: 29 April: promulgation of the law for the founding of the National Bank of Romania.

3f1318c9-403e-5af3-81fe-8bfc6d583567.name: Installation of the first electric telegraph lines
3f1318c9-403e-5af3-81fe-8bfc6d583567.description: 14 February: installation of the first electric telegraph lines in the Romanian territories, connecting Iaşi with Cernăuţi.

3f459cea-4de4-5170-a946-d8b9920ed268.name: Foundation of the School of Beaux-Arts
3f459cea-4de4-5170-a946-d8b9920ed268.description: 14 November: a School of Fine Arts (which today is the National University of Art) is founded in Bucharest by painters Gheorghe Tattarescu and Theodor Aman.

3f774691-8d6f-5415-b9a3-264764fe2d8e.name: Dona Branca
3f774691-8d6f-5415-b9a3-264764fe2d8e.description: Almeida Garrett writes the poems *Camões* (1825) and *Dona Branca* (1826), considered the first romantic works in Portuguese. The hero, Camões, is presented as an outcast who, returning to the motherland, dies in the year when Portugal loses its independence (1580). The fantasy of medieval wizardry traditions is represented in *Dona Branca*.

3f87cbe0-c2b9-5b76-b191-105dcbdde5c8.name: The Moorish Kiosk
3f87cbe0-c2b9-5b76-b191-105dcbdde5c8.description: The Moorish Kiosk, built for the World Exhibition in Paris in 1878, was subsequently bought for Linderhof Palace Park by Ludwig II. The Moroccan House, which was actually built in Morocco for the International Exhibition in Vienna in 1873 and acquired by a private individual after the king’s death, was bought by the German state in 1980 and reconstructed in the Palace Park in 1998.

3fa14438-b4b6-5f5c-890f-1c3481e4ceda.name: Italo-Turkish war
3fa14438-b4b6-5f5c-890f-1c3481e4ceda.description: Italo-Turkish war: Italy gains possession of Libya and the Dodecanese Islands.

3fd5e0cb-c3b5-56cb-911b-f8250f6e629c.name: Treaty of Lausanne
3fd5e0cb-c3b5-56cb-911b-f8250f6e629c.description: 24 July: Treaty of Lausanne, which officially dissolves the Ottoman Empire.

3fea2669-dee8-5d77-9463-064fb3c19684.name: Literacy rate
3fea2669-dee8-5d77-9463-064fb3c19684.description: Some 12 per cent of men and 20 per cent of women are unable to sign their marriage certificate because they cannot write, a considerable improvement in literacy rates since 1867.

3ff715c0-af5f-5dac-8f3b-ba9b52f1b3df.name: The emergence of musical nationalism
3ff715c0-af5f-5dac-8f3b-ba9b52f1b3df.description: The emergence of musical nationalism. Various musicians and composers, such as Isaac Albéniz, Enrique Granados and Manuel de Falla, develop musical styles identified with Spanish traditions and folklore, including flamenco.

41167463-bca6-5525-b15a-aaacc5f2c9f7.name: Emmanuel Roidis publishes his novel *Pope Joan*
41167463-bca6-5525-b15a-aaacc5f2c9f7.description: Emmanuel Roidis, one of Greece’s most influential authors, publishes his novel *Pope Joan*, which is translated into a number of languages.

4146062d-bd50-509e-9071-489a7fd73235.name: Oppositional weekly newspaper in London
4146062d-bd50-509e-9071-489a7fd73235.description: 29 June: Namık Kemal and Ziya Paşa publish oppositional weekly newspaper in London, where they had fled to.

4158faf2-bdc2-5dce-b596-c5084591557f.name: First World War
4158faf2-bdc2-5dce-b596-c5084591557f.description: World War I is declared and fought.

41790529-0380-5597-b8f7-e1d42ae74924.name: Filippo Marinetti
41790529-0380-5597-b8f7-e1d42ae74924.description: Filippo Marinetti publishes the Futurist Manifesto in *Le Figaro*.

419a27d9-f6c3-519e-b042-12e98c9e6d39.name: Karl Benz und Gottlieb Daimler invent the modern automobile
419a27d9-f6c3-519e-b042-12e98c9e6d39.description: Karl Benz and Gottlieb Daimler invent the modern automobile.

41aeaf8f-7731-5609-becc-f7165e986ca6.name: Septembrismo - the educational system reformed by Passos Manuel
41aeaf8f-7731-5609-becc-f7165e986ca6.description: Under Septembrismo the educational system is reformed by Passos Manuel (1801–62). To improve public education, the Plano Nacional dos Lyceus Nacionais equips each district capital with a *lyceu* (based on the French republican idea of *lycée*). The curriculum includes humanities and sciences and proposes an inductive and experimental learning process.

41e04dd5-0410-514b-a60e-a65a4960fad1.name: Alexandria Opera House
41e04dd5-0410-514b-a60e-a65a4960fad1.description: George Park begins building work on Alexandria Opera House, known also as Sayyid Darwish Theatre, which opens in 1921.

426811d5-e488-578e-bf2f-ed6b071df91f.name: First parliament in the German history is being established
426811d5-e488-578e-bf2f-ed6b071df91f.description: Establishment of the first parliament in German history (at the Paulskirche, Frankfurt am Main), and elaboration of the German Imperial Constitution.

42787100-c639-560d-b8bb-035d28f25390.name: Danilo I
42787100-c639-560d-b8bb-035d28f25390.description: Danilo I Prince of Montenegro is forced to leave his kingdom following its integration with Yugoslavia. He then seeks exile in Austria and dies in Vienna in 1939.

43104cfd-7a03-5b57-8e25-bb42f09233d5.name: Puccini's last opera *Turandot*
43104cfd-7a03-5b57-8e25-bb42f09233d5.description: Puccini’s last opera *Turandot*, which he left unfinished, is performed at La Scala in Milan under the direction of Arturo Toscanini.

432d66ee-9d55-5fe5-ab38-c22ca1daf30d.name: Beginning of the Greek immigration in Brăila
432d66ee-9d55-5fe5-ab38-c22ca1daf30d.description: The beginning of Greek immigration into Brăila. Many Greeks emigrate to Wallachia and settle in the Romanian ports on the Danube after the liberalisation of commerce on the Danube and Black Sea (1828).

433360bc-e2c9-5614-a09f-7d06bf6e2a56.name: A series of incidents provoke the intervention of the French army
433360bc-e2c9-5614-a09f-7d06bf6e2a56.description: A series of incidents provoke the intervention of the French army when in August 1907 the French land in Casablanca and occupy Oujda, Casablanca and Fez, despite opposition from Germany.

43813fa8-6aa0-512b-b99e-d1fc753f3a21.name: Foundation of the National Archaeological Museum of Athens
43813fa8-6aa0-512b-b99e-d1fc753f3a21.description: Foundation of the National Archaeological Museum of Athens.

43a7aa32-5095-5a82-8e5e-3e93825815ac.name: Parnassism
43a7aa32-5095-5a82-8e5e-3e93825815ac.description: Parnassism is a French literary style that grew up as a reaction to Romanticism. Advocating “Art for art's sake”, it rejected lyricism: Leconte de Lisle and José-Maria de Heredia are notable poets of this style.

4401b8da-9ed4-54f7-8c04-8c61eaf25f21.name: Free Institution for Education
4401b8da-9ed4-54f7-8c04-8c61eaf25f21.description: Following the curtailment of academic freedom in the university, a group of professors expelled from Madrid University introduces in Spain a new education system under the Institución Libre de Enseñanza (Free Institution for Education), a secular private project that would modernise all levels of the education system between 1876 and 1936. This initiative was to have an important impact on some of the most important Spanish intellectuals.

4475c342-c33a-5406-be52-89b3cdf8ac92.name: Foundation of the National Gallery in Athens
4475c342-c33a-5406-be52-89b3cdf8ac92.description: Foundation of the National Gallery in Athens. Its chief curator is the acclaimed painter Georgios Iakovidis.

448a4fcf-ecf7-502f-941c-6d390bca9871.name: The son of an Austrian General
448a4fcf-ecf7-502f-941c-6d390bca9871.description: The son of an Austrian general, Ferdinand of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha becomes King of Bulgaria; he leaves Bulgaria and immigrates to Germany in 1918.

44f3bdd1-57ac-53d1-84bd-d281dfd1202a.name: Increase of the foreign workers
44f3bdd1-57ac-53d1-84bd-d281dfd1202a.description: Foreign workers (especially from Austria-Hungary, Russia and Poland) arrive in the German Empire in increasing numbers to work in seasonal agriculture.

4500cecf-6397-5924-b9df-815925ebb0c8.name: Kinglake’s tour of the Middle East
4500cecf-6397-5924-b9df-815925ebb0c8.description: The development of steam power brings increased trade and travel to the eastern Mediterranean. This leads to the publication of travel literature and an interest in the archaeology of the Bible. A. W. Kinglake’s *Eothen* is the most widely read of the travel books.

450abbe7-374e-5d3f-9c53-ccac9a6e1b3e.name: Likewise its European counterparts
450abbe7-374e-5d3f-9c53-ccac9a6e1b3e.description: Inauguration of the Escola de Medicina Tropical de Lisboa (Lisbon Academy of Tropical Medicine), founded like its European counterparts to provide specialised training, spread knowledge and undertake field research. One of its main subjects was sleeping sickness for whose treatment the Academy undertook five field missions (1904–11) to São Tomé and Mozambique.

455df1fc-7f8d-5efe-97db-15681e3f982e.name: The Royal and Parliamentary Titles Act
455df1fc-7f8d-5efe-97db-15681e3f982e.description: The Royal and Parliamentary Titles Act renames parliament to reflect the change following secession of Southern Ireland. The state is now known as the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

457106c2-fa6e-50d8-b486-320d95395c15.name: First Chambers of Labour
457106c2-fa6e-50d8-b486-320d95395c15.description: First Chambers of Labour (territorial trade unions) founded in Milan.

45d4981a-358e-5110-a4e0-13ca98ea6ad4.name: The official working day 8 hours
45d4981a-358e-5110-a4e0-13ca98ea6ad4.description: The official working day is recognised as eight hours; the official working week is set at 48 hours.

45db51c1-d06a-5cb2-8c25-83aaa5309e9e.name: The first Macedonian composer Atanas Badev
45db51c1-d06a-5cb2-8c25-83aaa5309e9e.description: The birth in Prilep of the first Macedonian composer Atanas Badev (d. 1908). He studied music in Russia and was conductor of several school choirs and of the first city choir in Prilep.

46268f65-5171-5eae-ad1a-93776d42efb0.name: The Lebanese buy homes from the Italians and Jews
46268f65-5171-5eae-ad1a-93776d42efb0.description: The Lebanese buy homes from the Italians and Jews, who are moving away. They learn about clothes, home improvements, insurance and credit. Businesses are branching out, with dry goods and notions business replaced by grocery stores, butcher shops, coffee houses and sales of farm produce from vehicles.

4668180a-03f9-5e6a-8b6b-b7d7b11fa5d3.name: The beginning of the Madrid subway system
4668180a-03f9-5e6a-8b6b-b7d7b11fa5d3.description: The beginning of the Madrid subway system, the first in Spain, heralding a major advance in public transport in cities.

46727e50-99db-5235-9062-ed754fc0fcfe.name: Approximately 400,000 Greeks emigrate to America
46727e50-99db-5235-9062-ed754fc0fcfe.description: Approximately 400,000 Greeks migrate to America due to widespread unemployment and economic problems.

4683d8b5-b3dd-5bd2-a15b-82540f947507.name: Chemist Julius Lothar Meyer develops periodical system
4683d8b5-b3dd-5bd2-a15b-82540f947507.description: The chemist Julius Lothar Meyer (1830–95) develops the first periodic table of chemical elements.

46a709ec-c148-5bd9-b14d-1b50743e9a63.name: The creation of Sadiki College
46a709ec-c148-5bd9-b14d-1b50743e9a63.description: The creation of Sadiki College based on a modern concept of education: the school separates from the mosque and a distinction is made between educational structures and those of the religious life.

46b02563-57d3-5b63-b95d-4ca37ce1335a.name: The popular uprising
46b02563-57d3-5b63-b95d-4ca37ce1335a.description: The popular uprising sounds the death knell for reform. The great figure of this insurrection, ‘Ali bin Ghedham, comes from the region of Kasserine.

472d3156-e5df-5b37-bd7e-f55225ad1cec.name: Moroccan resistance
472d3156-e5df-5b37-bd7e-f55225ad1cec.description: Moroccan resistance is spirited, and provokes many Berber revolts. Following the surrender of Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Alkrim, who led the peasant revolts in the Rif (1919–26), France launched a campaign of “pacification” that lasted until 1934.

476f3dd9-7c8b-5af2-ba6d-77cf7cca2828.name: Birth of Pablo Picasso in Málaga
476f3dd9-7c8b-5af2-ba6d-77cf7cca2828.description: Birth of Pablo Picasso in Málaga. In Spain Picasso’s birth date would be established as the boundary between works of art in the Academic style and the avant-garde style.

4776d249-78f9-5f01-9189-4a269a6d9186.name: Gaetano Donizetti and Vincenzo Bellini
4776d249-78f9-5f01-9189-4a269a6d9186.description: Once Rossini has left the stage, his place is taken by Gaetano Donizetti (1797–1848) and Vincenzo Bellini (1801–1835). They introduce the new romantic spirit into melodrama and establish a tighter link between words and music. Their style is characterised by greater attention to the psychology of the different characters.

47bc4860-e989-5190-b3f5-711c0f89f6da.name: First edition of the Milano Fair
47bc4860-e989-5190-b3f5-711c0f89f6da.description: First Milan Fair of industrial products: 1,233 exhibitors (including 224 foreigners) and 360,000 visitors.

47f2716b-c277-5d0a-9574-aa843100d4ef.name: School of Law
47f2716b-c277-5d0a-9574-aa843100d4ef.description: A Law School is established during Isma‘il Pasha’s era in 1868. Known then as the School of Management and Languages, the two schools separate in 1882 and remain as such until July 1886. That year, it becomes the School of Law with two departments, primary and high.

48adfaa5-0d40-5cae-838c-35c03cef5f52.name: The earliest Turkish textbook on chemistry
48adfaa5-0d40-5cae-838c-35c03cef5f52.description: The earliest Turkish textbook on chemistry, *Usul-i Kimya* (Elements of chemistry), is written by Mehmed Emin Derviş Paşa, a graduate of the Military Engineering School in Istanbul, based on the chemistry books he used during his studies in the École des Mines in Paris.

48b00a4a-73ce-5b7b-a03a-131640f7d06c.name: Lord Curzon visits the Arab Gulf sheikhdoms
48b00a4a-73ce-5b7b-a03a-131640f7d06c.description: Age 42, a young and energetic Viceroy of India, Lord Curzon, visits the Arab Gulf sheikhdoms to confirm treaties of British protection of them, a policy that prevails until 1970.

48c095ca-e0b5-5e7b-bd8f-6effc1a4f268.name: Excavations in Troy
48c095ca-e0b5-5e7b-bd8f-6effc1a4f268.description: English amateur archaeologist Frank Calvert (1828–1908) begins excavations in Troy.

48eb539b-1590-5c94-91ce-6df29b204901.name: French Romanticism
48eb539b-1590-5c94-91ce-6df29b204901.description: The Romantic movement develops at the beginning of the 19th century under the influence of writers such as François-René de Chateaubriand. The movement, inspired by imagination, individualism, a taste for the outrageous, and exoticism, is marked by the poetry of Alphonse de Lamartine and Victor Hugo and then extends to the theatre with Hugo’s masterpiece *Battle of Hernani*, and then to literature. Hugo was the uncontested leader of this literary movement. Music and dance were both influenced by Romanticism; in choreography and in costume design (the tutu and points) the feminine was accentuated.

492aefc2-7c81-53be-a5b4-10079f5fbdf7.name: First Italian National Industrial Exhibition in Milan
492aefc2-7c81-53be-a5b4-10079f5fbdf7.description: The first Italian National Industrial Exhibition is held in Milan.

497f518d-0cb6-55fc-8819-22c800616754.name: Luísa Todi
497f518d-0cb6-55fc-8819-22c800616754.description: The death of Luísa Todi (b. 1753), the most celebrated mezzo-soprano opera singer in Portugal. Luísa began her musical career when she was 14 years old. She performed in major European cities and was invited to perform in the courts of Catherine of Russia and Frederick William of Prussia.

49b1ea1c-4154-5de9-a06e-f7b48091e1e2.name: Romania becomes part of the Triple Alliance
49b1ea1c-4154-5de9-a06e-f7b48091e1e2.description: 30 October: by signing a treaty with Austro-Hungary, to which Germany adheres the same day and Italy in 1888, Romania becomes part of the Triple Alliance.

4a2ef575-715c-516e-9851-ae5671e7f184.name: Development of the Minas de Riotinto
4a2ef575-715c-516e-9851-ae5671e7f184.description: Development of the Minas de Riotinto (Huelva, Andalucía). Bought by a British company, the mines bring important economic progress to this region. The dangerous chemicals used in metal extraction spark the first environmental protest by mine workers. (The first fooball match took place in this mine, thanks to the British engineers.)

4a39af34-47d2-5b95-9bc0-e368cab023ca.name: At the congress of Berlin in June 1878
4a39af34-47d2-5b95-9bc0-e368cab023ca.description: In June the signatories at the Congress of Berlin grant Austria the right to occupy and fully administer Bosnia and Herzegovina for an undetermined period.

4a3fee6f-c931-5881-b439-7a8942be880d.name: Enlivement of the capital market
4a3fee6f-c931-5881-b439-7a8942be880d.description: The capital market is enlivened by France’s payment of 5 million French francs, paid to Germany as compensation following the war between the two countries (1870–1).

4ac60b1d-a50f-558f-903a-190c9d19fff7.name: The Sanssouci Palace in Potsdam is connected to Berlin by rail
4ac60b1d-a50f-558f-903a-190c9d19fff7.description: The Sanssouci Palace in Potsdam is connected to Berlin by rail, one of the first electrified railway sections in Old Germany. Since 1911, the Palace has been used as a film location (i.e. *The Blue Angel*, 1930).

4b3e43a7-e496-5409-8c07-db01e7254205.name: Travels in the Near East
4b3e43a7-e496-5409-8c07-db01e7254205.description: A. W. Kinglake’s *Eothen* is the best known of the many travel books to the East. William M. Thackeray, Benjamin Disraeli and Anthony Trollope all travel to the Near East, others wander around Asia Minor and the Levant recording their impressions, often in search of classical inscriptions.

4b7c3e3a-f10b-5b3b-8e96-4a897decad5f.name: The Maison de Art nouveau
4b7c3e3a-f10b-5b3b-8e96-4a897decad5f.description: The Maison de l'Art nouveau by Samuel Bing.

4bd72f7a-017a-58b5-8def-a149753159ca.name: First state confiscation and sale of Church properties
4bd72f7a-017a-58b5-8def-a149753159ca.description: First state confiscation and sale of Church properties known, after the minister who developed the law, as Desamortización de Mendizábal (Mendizábal's Disentailment) to fund the Carlist war.

4be5bc72-2162-5667-a414-541727dc487e.name: Cote Azur
4be5bc72-2162-5667-a414-541727dc487e.description: The birth of the French Riviera, originally frequented by wealthy English patrons.

4c54dec5-c9b5-5fd0-83d1-69613a9e8de6.name: Rumi calendar
4c54dec5-c9b5-5fd0-83d1-69613a9e8de6.description: Official recognition of the Mâli Takvim (Rumi calendar) as the second calendar system alongside the Hijra calendar.

4c65d23b-f203-5a13-a315-389c63919cac.name: The population of Sharjah town
4c65d23b-f203-5a13-a315-389c63919cac.description: In around 1800, the Sharjah town is estimated to have around 2,000 to 3,000 inhabitants.

4c9dbae5-fd84-5b4b-be95-fe2895b346b0.name: Work weekly rest compulsory
4c9dbae5-fd84-5b4b-be95-fe2895b346b0.description: Introduction of a compulsory weekly rest period of 24 hours (voted on 3 July).

4ca5e1f7-7de9-5afe-b43d-5b1ad4928582.name: The Iliou Melathron built by architect Ernst Ziller
4ca5e1f7-7de9-5afe-b43d-5b1ad4928582.description: The Iliou Melathron is designed by architect Ernst Ziller as the residence of the archaeologist Heinrich Schliemann and his family.

4cc37d68-882f-5814-a5d0-d7374055dd43.name: The restoration of the Aqueduct of Zaghouan
4cc37d68-882f-5814-a5d0-d7374055dd43.description: The restoration of the Aqueduct of Zaghouan is completed, running water arrives in Tunis.

4ccc7d4c-0804-5cf5-af20-e601367cc584.name: Arrival of refugees
4ccc7d4c-0804-5cf5-af20-e601367cc584.description: Many thousands of refugees arrive from Asia Minor.

4d0d093b-645d-5797-b6f9-4daee2b367c0.name: Inauguration of the Luxor-Aswan railway
4d0d093b-645d-5797-b6f9-4daee2b367c0.description: On 4 December, in the city of Luxor, the Minister of Transportation, Muhammad Mahmud along with a group of Ministers inaugurates the Luxor–Aswan Railway. The railway is considered one of Mahmud Pasha’s greatest accomplishments as Minister of Transportation.

4d28b8b4-0de7-5258-9527-b26280b8e59b.name: Steamship company Fevâid-I Osmâniyye
4d28b8b4-0de7-5258-9527-b26280b8e59b.description: Steamship company Fevâid-I Osmâniyye is founded.

4da1b1f1-7506-57d0-8146-2efb10ecabfb.name: The Alexandrian poet Cavafy publishes the poem *Ithaca*
4da1b1f1-7506-57d0-8146-2efb10ecabfb.description: The Alexandrian poet Constantine P. Cavafy publishes his poem *Ithaca*.

4dc5a0b8-04a6-512d-ac75-6ef210a6a2cb.name: Creation of the United Principalities of Wallachia and Moldavia
4dc5a0b8-04a6-512d-ac75-6ef210a6a2cb.description: 19 August: the Ottoman Empire, Austria, Russia, Prussia, Piedmont, the UK and France sign the Paris Convention marking the creation of the United Principalities of Wallachia and Moldavia, with separate rulers, legislative and executive powers, and only two institutions in common (Supreme Court of Appeals and central legislative commission). The convention replaces the Organic Regulations, becoming the new constitution of the United Principalities.

4dd015c9-34bf-551c-b584-d072c3d9fc51.name: In 1853 started the War of Krimaia
4dd015c9-34bf-551c-b584-d072c3d9fc51.description: The Crimean War starts in October 1853. On one side is the Russian Empire and on the other the Ottoman Empire, the British Empire, France and the Kingdom of Sardinia. Greece participates with a volunteer corps of 1,000 men as one of Russia’s few allies.

4e1fd90e-03c9-5ff1-921b-672b52c32f8b.name: Genesis of the most popular classic compositions
4e1fd90e-03c9-5ff1-921b-672b52c32f8b.description: The era marks the genesis of some of the world’s most popular classical compositions, for example: in 1841 Robert Schumann composes *Frühlingssinfonie* (Spring Symphony) and in 1859 Johannes Brahms finished the concerto *Klavierkonzert Nr.1d-Moll op.15* (Piano Concerto No. 1 in D minor, Op.15). In 1889 Gustav Mahler’s *1\. Sinfonie D-Dur* (Symphony No. 1 in D major) is premiered; followed in 1905 by his *Kindertotenlieder* (Songs on the Death of Children).

4e477f9f-7e9e-5b5f-98d2-f95c52c6274c.name: Development and rearmament
4e477f9f-7e9e-5b5f-98d2-f95c52c6274c.description: Development and rearmament (*Aufrüstung*) of the German Navy.

4e53cab6-b4f5-5bf4-b886-91bb102f5f54.name: Ottoman Empire obtains its first foreign loan
4e53cab6-b4f5-5bf4-b886-91bb102f5f54.description: Ottoman Empire obtains its first foreign loan.

4e7969bb-a12c-5660-bf3b-ee60143901bc.name: Law confiscates the properties of religious orders
4e7969bb-a12c-5660-bf3b-ee60143901bc.description: A law confiscates the properties of religious orders and congregations, and establishes a state fund to support the clergy and monks.

4e7ceac9-496f-530a-b3a6-6da81ccd6df5.name: Revolution of February
4e7ceac9-496f-530a-b3a6-6da81ccd6df5.description: Revolution of February 1848: Louis-Philippe abdicates and the Republic is proclaimed.

4e93cc09-17e7-5569-bac4-9f0f7b94a32f.name: Mulay Sulayman and trade policy
4e93cc09-17e7-5569-bac4-9f0f7b94a32f.description: In relation to trade policy, Mulay Sulayman opposes the liberalism of his father Muhammad Ibn ‘Abd Allah by passing an edict in 1814 imposing a 50 per cent duty on imports, and takes restrictive measures by banning the export of most Moroccan commodities to Europe, including grain, oil, wool, animal hides and livestock. The years of drought and swarms of locusts that devastated all crops between 1810 and 1816 caused a shortage of basic commodities, price increases and famine, on top of the plague epidemics that swept the country. All of these factors necessarily weakened the country financially and demographically. This could help to explain the inward-looking policies adopted by the sovereign Mulay Sulayman, who—according to some historical sources—claimed that he did not need Europe and hoped that Europe did not need him. A desperate and exhausted Mulay Sulayman resigned and chose his nephew Mulay ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hisham as his successor.

4e9a6421-6cab-5986-9b44-409d532333e5.name: The dam of Artzan-Amatovo in Kilkis
4e9a6421-6cab-5986-9b44-409d532333e5.description: Building of the Arzan-Amatovo Dam in Kilkis.

4ebeba31-8816-51af-a637-071730167e9c.name: The buildings are architecturally innovative
4ebeba31-8816-51af-a637-071730167e9c.description: Buildings present innovation in their architecture, decoration and positioning. Palaces, patrician houses and mosques incorporate elements of Baroque style; new European techniques and decorative touches that recall Italian arts are evident at the same time as the increased use of foreign labour.

4ee660c6-7eff-5dd0-abd0-0c51be0b78fc.name: Kasper von Zumbusch starts with the building of the monument of Empress Maria Theresia
4ee660c6-7eff-5dd0-abd0-0c51be0b78fc.description: Kasper von Zumbusch (1830–1915) begins work on a monument to Empress Maria Theresia, situated on Maria-Theresien-Platz at the Ringstrasse in Vienna.

4f112add-7ae3-559e-b635-19c2c5c3b088.name: Crinoline
4f112add-7ae3-559e-b635-19c2c5c3b088.description: The crinoline underskirt increases the volume of women’s skirts.

4f2314ae-0a25-546f-96ac-bb91c56b264d.name: Greece has a small stand at the Great Exhibition in London
4f2314ae-0a25-546f-96ac-bb91c56b264d.description: Greece is represented by a small stand at the Great Exhibition in London among the Levantine states.

4f4821d8-4fc4-5539-9381-abc32c175b40.name: Sykes-Picot Agreements
4f4821d8-4fc4-5539-9381-abc32c175b40.description: British interests in the Middle East are driven partly by the British Indian administration and partly by the strategic alliance with France. Mark Sykes for Britain and George Picot for France come to a diplomatic agreement to divide the Ottoman Levantine possessions for their respective countries. This conflicts with an earlier British promise of independence.

4fa5b084-ccee-51a0-888e-441a0eadc4e7.name: Second empire becomesmore liberal
4fa5b084-ccee-51a0-888e-441a0eadc4e7.description: After an authoritarian period (1852–60), during which time freedoms are severely restricted and political opponents are forced into exile, the Second Empire is declared and the political climate becomes more liberal and the economy grows.

4fcd3cd1-44d9-5873-afd8-a1b14360d876.name: Land Law
4fcd3cd1-44d9-5873-afd8-a1b14360d876.description: 6 June: Promulgation of the Land Law regulating private property in agricultural areas.

502cbc51-2afa-5031-bc79-3309e0b3aa1b.name: First thermoelectric power station
502cbc51-2afa-5031-bc79-3309e0b3aa1b.description: In Milan, the first thermoelectric power station in Europe is inaugurated.

504efb9b-7a83-52e3-8fd0-af51ba48fa52.name: Khedive Ismail paid a visit to Britain

507640d5-645b-5b9e-9049-245800b5c547.name: First Egyptian stamps
507640d5-645b-5b9e-9049-245800b5c547.description: The first Egyptian stamps are issued on 1 January.

507e350f-8160-54f3-898e-0abc4c0f2099.name: Shipping line between Alexandria and Marseille
507e350f-8160-54f3-898e-0abc4c0f2099.description: Opening of shipping routes between Alexandria and Marseille.

50fbf1e7-f901-5a61-a71a-18153a863439.name: Ludwig the second
50fbf1e7-f901-5a61-a71a-18153a863439.description: Ludwig II (r. 1864–86) had several palaces built during his reign. The most famous among these are Neuschwanenstein (1868–92, still in construction when Ludwig died), Neues Schloss Herrenchiemsee (1878–86, built along the lines of Versailles, but never completed), and Linderhof (1869–85), the only palace the king lived to see completed.

511ce86e-19e7-5ace-969b-b24404fb8218.name: The Ottoman Sultan Abdulhamid built the Hijaz Railway
511ce86e-19e7-5ace-969b-b24404fb8218.description: Under the Ottoman Sultan ‘Abd al-Hamid, the Hijaz Railway is built, running from Istanbul to the Medina (Madinah) province.

51238758-1250-51d0-b39b-c394ee0ab829.name: Promulgation of the law for a new monetary system and national coins
51238758-1250-51d0-b39b-c394ee0ab829.description: 4 May: proclamation of the law for the introduction of a new monetary system and for the issuing of national coins; 1870 is the year when the first Romanian coins are minted in Romania having previously been minted abroad.

515c9e8e-094c-5267-905d-66751069fc9b.name: *Antigüedades Árabes de España* published by Real Academia de Bellas Artes
515c9e8e-094c-5267-905d-66751069fc9b.description: *Antigüedades Árabes de España* published by Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando – it marks the beginning of the rediscovery of the Arab past.

5168cd8e-da5d-5964-9320-4829c8ab19b4.name: The earliest portrait which was not part of religious depiction
5168cd8e-da5d-5964-9320-4829c8ab19b4.description: The earliest portrait in Macedonian art that is not part of religious depiction, a portrait of a child is painted by Dimitar Andonov of Papradishte (1859–1954). Dimitar Andonov was one of the last Macedonian “zographs” (icon painters) and the founder of Macedonian profane art.

5171be65-2fdc-5d89-bb75-5cc0cf543cd1.name: Building of a telephone network in Vienna
5171be65-2fdc-5d89-bb75-5cc0cf543cd1.description: Designs for a telephone network in Vienna.

51bf24d4-5b82-54c4-aa31-6dec827ec632.name: Mariano Fortuny y Madrazo designs dresses, cloaks and tunics influenced by Arab and North African garments
51bf24d4-5b82-54c4-aa31-6dec827ec632.description: Mariano Fortuny y Madrazo designs dresses, cloaks and tunics influenced by Arab and North African garments such as the *abas* or the *bournous*. He is best known for his dresses inspired by the garments of Antiquity such as his Delphos dresses, or in the orientalist style.

52039ee7-a368-5300-b523-8d726bfe3f91.name: German industrial production
52039ee7-a368-5300-b523-8d726bfe3f91.description: Germany’s industrial production is now six times what it had been.

52423f27-01cf-54d6-8756-16a3e3dae70b.name: Beaufort Castle
52423f27-01cf-54d6-8756-16a3e3dae70b.description: The Galilee earthquake. In the 17th century, Fakhr-al-Din II took over Beaufort castle, but was defeated by the Ottomans who destroyed the upper portion. The earthquake causes further damage to the structure and the ruins become a quarry and a shelter for sheep.

526938cd-a1ad-5502-b1e0-8baba34b9223.name: Otto von Bismarck becomes Prussian prime minister
526938cd-a1ad-5502-b1e0-8baba34b9223.description: Otto von Bismarck becomes prime minister of Prussia.

528e0cac-864b-501b-bb79-f876f67c7c8a.name: A Neo-Manuelin architectural style for the Pavilion of Portugal
528e0cac-864b-501b-bb79-f876f67c7c8a.description: At the “Exposition Universelle” in Paris, the Portugal Pavilion employs a neo-Manueline architectural style. The exoticism is a symbol of the Portuguese Empire built by the discoveries of the 15th and 16th centuries.

52b85841-4d43-5c07-b956-e414fefed5b2.name: Building of a hospital known as the military infirmary
52b85841-4d43-5c07-b956-e414fefed5b2.description: Sultan ‘Abd al-‘Aziz orders the building of a hospital known as the military infirmary. It will later be turned into a courthouse after the French Mandate and then become the Insitute of Fine Arts of the Lebanese University.

53b48100-e096-59b6-a2e8-0b24bcee1519.name: Unified silver currency in the Austrian Hungarian empire
53b48100-e096-59b6-a2e8-0b24bcee1519.description: A unified silver currency the Guilder (Gulden) is introduced throughout the Austrian-Hungarian Empire.

53ea5d1e-6589-5473-abc2-37eb450a38d0.name: Visit of Ottoman Sultan to France and Britain
53ea5d1e-6589-5473-abc2-37eb450a38d0.description: The 1850s and 1860s sees close political, commercial and cultural relations between the Ottoman Empire and Britain. The zenith of this relationship is the state visit of Ottoman Sultan ‘Abd al-‘Aziz to France and then Britain. The Prince of Wales then reciprocates with a visit to Constantinople, Damascus and Jerusalem in 1869.

53f03dfb-b290-578b-855a-bf52873c37f7.name: English archaeologist and politician Austen Henry Layard
53f03dfb-b290-578b-855a-bf52873c37f7.description: English archaeologist and politician Austen Henry Layard (1817–94) publishes *Nineveh and its Remains*.

53f10eda-cd6b-5602-929c-5db7c9ebcf07.name: Migration to Australia
53f10eda-cd6b-5602-929c-5db7c9ebcf07.description: A group of about a dozen Lebanese, dissatisfied with the dismal prospect of earning a livelihood from the stubborn northern Lebanese soil, set out to stake their claim on the mythical riches in the new land of Australia.

540ede32-4d44-58c4-a200-3d42e34dc8b8.name: The last palace
540ede32-4d44-58c4-a200-3d42e34dc8b8.description: The last palace (*Cicilienhof*) of the House of Hohenzollern (a dynasty of former princes, electors, kings and emperors) was built under Wilhelm II. The palace hosted the Conference of Potsdam in 1945.

543d39c0-e904-57c1-b4b1-7d600ad4ebd1.name: Athens becomes the capital of the new established State
543d39c0-e904-57c1-b4b1-7d600ad4ebd1.description: Athens becomes the capital of the newly established state.

54522e7d-6a84-57c8-92bb-bbe36339a303.name: Media critical of British politics penetrate the Trucial Coast
54522e7d-6a84-57c8-92bb-bbe36339a303.description: Media from Egypt and India critical of British politics penetrates the Trucial Coast. The Cairo-based newspapers *Al-Mu’ayyad* and *Al-Liwa* have numerous subscribers on the Trucial Coast.

5480a2e9-b3cf-5698-8812-798710f49173.name: World War I
5480a2e9-b3cf-5698-8812-798710f49173.description: On 25 July, at the onset of World War I, ‘Abbas Hilmi II is in Constantinople where he suffers wounds to his hands and cheeks during a failed assassination attempt. On 5 November of that same year, when Britain declares war on Turkey, ‘Abbas is accused of deserting his country because he did not return home forthwith. In addition, because the British believe that he has been plotting against their rule, when the Ottoman Empire joins the central powers in the war, Britain declares Egypt an independent Sultanate under British Protectorate on 18 December, and ‘Abbas is deposed.

5490ae09-bc60-56a1-be1d-40ce47ab45bc.name: Collection of short stories considered the Naturalist manifesto
5490ae09-bc60-56a1-be1d-40ce47ab45bc.description: The *Soirées de Médan*, a collection of short stories by Guy de Maupassant, Émile Zola, etc., is considered to be the Naturalist manifesto.

55322a1f-4a7c-5812-ab3d-c2b2a5101dd3.name: Opening of the Isabel II channel
55322a1f-4a7c-5812-ab3d-c2b2a5101dd3.description: Opening of the Isabel II channel, the water system of Madrid diverting water from the river Lozoya to the new fountain in San Bernardo street in the centre of Madrid.

553de630-835e-58f5-9cb8-cf2c1f333d0b.name: Setembrismo - Lower middle classes rebellion and fight against corruption and higher middle class privileges
553de630-835e-58f5-9cb8-cf2c1f333d0b.description: Period of Setembrismo: lower-middle-class rebellion against corruption and upper-middle-class privileges. An industrialisation process takes off to counteract foreign dominance. To overcome the loss of Brazilian revenues the colonisation of African possessions is boosted. The slave trade is prohibited in 1836 by abolitionist Marquis of Sá da Bandeira.

555835b4-7e17-5ac4-94aa-94b7bd74a0b2.name: Foundation Stone of the University of Fuad I
555835b4-7e17-5ac4-94aa-94b7bd74a0b2.description: Laying of the Foundation Stone of the University of Fuad I.

559148d2-07ca-5cb2-a72c-19fa7da07c0e.name: Russian-Ottoman war
559148d2-07ca-5cb2-a72c-19fa7da07c0e.description: After the Russian–Ottoman war of 1806–12 Russia annexes the eastern part of Moldavia (Bessarabia).

55c7a34e-587d-55d9-b4af-ea04ceb27fcb.name: Legislation on women's and children's work
55c7a34e-587d-55d9-b4af-ea04ceb27fcb.description: Legislation passed prohibiting children under the age of 12 from working, women from working in mines and under-age women from working at night. First provisions for maternity leave (four weeks after delivery).

55dc1e5f-3de3-54f1-8d2b-f0f8816af85c.name: With the 1st World War
55dc1e5f-3de3-54f1-8d2b-f0f8816af85c.description: With the outbreak of World War I, the modernist movement thrives in Portugal with the return from France of a group of avant-garde artists including the painters Manuel Bentes (1885–1961), Eduardo Viana (1881–1967), José Pacheko (1885–1934) and Amadeo de Souza Cardoso, and the sculptors Diogo de Macedo (1889–1959), and Francisco Franco (1885–1955).

56918d66-0150-5b58-9966-4337f8888f24.name: Abbas Hilmi II paid a visit to Britain
56918d66-0150-5b58-9966-4337f8888f24.description: On a visit to Britain, ‘Abbas Hilmi II tells the authorities that he thinks the British have carried out good work in Egypt. He declares himself ready to cooperate with British officials administering Egypt and Sudan.

569c392a-b568-5306-bb00-d1f16663592a.name: Mihri Müşfik Hanım, one of the first female painters
569c392a-b568-5306-bb00-d1f16663592a.description: 26 February: Mihri Müşfik Hanım, one of the first female painters of renown, is born.

56b7ed64-eb48-563b-9657-5ac3c9528ec0.name: Italian migration to France
56b7ed64-eb48-563b-9657-5ac3c9528ec0.description: First wave of Italian immigrants to France.

56d7e7ed-4464-5031-9d6d-2a774bfd2d27.name: The first Italian telephone services
56d7e7ed-4464-5031-9d6d-2a774bfd2d27.description: The first Italian telephone services run by private companies start operating.

56fcc497-e0fe-5985-81cf-14538ebf4baa.name: Sharjah town
56fcc497-e0fe-5985-81cf-14538ebf4baa.description: Sharjah is recorded as having 175 stone buildings and 2,000 *areesh* (palm-frond) houses.

57284fdf-b4c9-5d0e-a359-44d020aa08f5.name: Labour Day
57284fdf-b4c9-5d0e-a359-44d020aa08f5.description: On 1 May, Labour Day is celebrated for the first time.

572d21b7-7e6c-5d4c-b128-c2dbd824adb4.name: Khedive Ismail visits Paris and London
572d21b7-7e6c-5d4c-b128-c2dbd824adb4.description: Khedive Isma‘il Pasha visits Paris and then London, where he is received by Queen Victoria and welcomed by the Lord Mayor. He attends a British Royal Navy fleet review alongside the Ottoman Sultan.

574ef8d1-bdb5-52b9-961a-33fc61639c5b.name: The Realist movement
574ef8d1-bdb5-52b9-961a-33fc61639c5b.description: The Realist movement, which emerges as a reaction to Classicism, focuses on the faithful representation of daily life in both town and country and particularly affects literature and painting.

57a47f0b-50b9-51c4-9324-ddb854b95650.name: The Picnic on the Grass
57a47f0b-50b9-51c4-9324-ddb854b95650.description: *The Picnic on the Grass* by Édouard Manet marks a transition from Realism to Impressionism

57b42694-27f9-5726-bbe6-caf3bdbead10.name: Railway network
57b42694-27f9-5726-bbe6-caf3bdbead10.description: Development of a railway network connecting the city of Tunis with its hinterland.

57dc1bd7-0613-5e19-b461-a9bd35428907.name: Columbano Bordalo Pinheiro
57dc1bd7-0613-5e19-b461-a9bd35428907.description: *O Grupo Do Leão* painted by Columbano Bordalo Pinheiro is a landmark in 19th-century painting both for its quality and for its subject matter. The depicted group of artists in the *Leão* beer house were linked to the Portuguese Naturalist and Realist painting movement. This work became famous and marked the beginning of a period of great artistic activity.

5823b3de-647d-5edf-b275-d2e87272f359.name: Development of steam power in the early nineteenth century also applied to marine transport
5823b3de-647d-5edf-b275-d2e87272f359.description: The development of steam power in the early 19th century also applies to marine transport. Steamships shorten distances, but they also require fuelling stations. In 1839, Britain acquires Aden as one fuelling station on the route to India.
