cdb3e04e-f30f-55b1-a99c-9798b4c55636.name: Factory Gas Boavista, owned by Lisbonense Gaslight Company
cdb3e04e-f30f-55b1-a99c-9798b4c55636.description: Boavista gas factory, owned by Companhia Lisbonense de Iluminação a Gás, begins to operate Lisbon's lightning network. Fearing people's reaction to a gas factory in an urban area, a styled façade is erected in 1856 to disguise it.

cdf9940a-81ce-5846-840d-f1fc8b0691b1.name: Anarchist Gaetano Bresci kills the King Umberto I
cdf9940a-81ce-5846-840d-f1fc8b0691b1.description: Anarchist Gaetano Bresci kills the King Umberto I, in revenge for the protesters killed in Milan in 1898. Victor Emanuel III becomes King of Italy.

ce232266-2e3c-5daf-9b41-7c03abc2cb40.name: Different circular letters by the Minister of Interior place obstacles on migration
ce232266-2e3c-5daf-9b41-7c03abc2cb40.description: Different circular letters by the Minister of Interior place obstacles on migration: migrants are supposed to have work contracts or to prove they have enough funding to repatriate. Such circular letters have only limited effect. Landowners put pressure on government to discourage migration.

ce2db643-ac7b-51b3-a1ce-f04c5e23cf50.name: The amount of buildings and mobile heritage collected from the confiscations
ce2db643-ac7b-51b3-a1ce-f04c5e23cf50.description: The buildings and portable heritage collected from the confiscations are sold in public auction to an emergent new aristocracy and a newly empowered upper middle class and the proceeds used to fund part of the state deficit.

ce7f7725-a11d-5927-8bf5-2308b4754c2e.name: The Italian State buys the 15th-century building of Villa Borghese in Rome
ce7f7725-a11d-5927-8bf5-2308b4754c2e.description: The Italian state buys the 15th-century building of Villa Borghese in Rome and the park around it, including the astounding collection of paintings and sculptures that the villa housed. The villa will be transformed into the Borghese Gallery and Museum.

ce881312-2ffb-50e9-a35d-02ba7c325cdf.name: British, French and other European arms dealers
ce881312-2ffb-50e9-a35d-02ba7c325cdf.description: By 1899 private British, French and other European arms dealers import some 20,000 rifles into the Trucial Coast region and Oman annually.

cec2284b-4393-5b0a-8820-b272d1406ef9.name: Gründerkrise
cec2284b-4393-5b0a-8820-b272d1406ef9.description: The economic crash known as the *Gründerkrise* sees companies and banks shut down and a rise in unemployment and social dissatisfaction.

cedc161c-030e-5881-babf-9d0d68b9c68b.name: The Treaty of Adrianople
cedc161c-030e-5881-babf-9d0d68b9c68b.description: The Treaty of Adrianople, following a Russian-Turkish war, opens up the Black Sea to international trade. Trebizond becomes a major port for Persia and India. Constantinople, Smyrna (Izmir) and Aleppo, which have been major international trading communities for many centuries now, flourish with the expansion of steam power.

cf0923ae-1eb5-53c9-add3-a2c73c86da01.name: Society for German Colonization
cf0923ae-1eb5-53c9-add3-a2c73c86da01.description: The goal in founding the Society for German Colonization was to acquire colonial territories overseas.

cf221b77-8c96-5dca-bd70-d1867ad91ae0.name: Fausto Zonaro
cf221b77-8c96-5dca-bd70-d1867ad91ae0.description: Fausto Zonaro (1854–1929) arrives in İstanbul as an independent artist. He receives the title of court painter in 1896.

cf705c27-2f78-5f54-b8d3-692bef0195ad.name: 2.251.463 people migrate from Italy
cf705c27-2f78-5f54-b8d3-692bef0195ad.description: 2,251,463 people migrate from Italy; 67 per cent of them go to the USA.

cf7629ca-daa6-5361-abca-22273c761e10.name: British declare the independence of Egypt
cf7629ca-daa6-5361-abca-22273c761e10.description: Britain declares Egyptian independence, but retains control of Egyptian foreign policy and the basic administration of the country. On 15 March of this year, Fuad I issues a decree changing his title from Sultan of Egypt to King of Egypt.

cfa5df40-cf49-58d8-8b27-9753dce16842.name: Müfide Kadri
cfa5df40-cf49-58d8-8b27-9753dce16842.description: Müfide Kadri is born (d. 1912). One of the early female painters, she took private classes from Osman Hamdi Bey.

d017cc8e-acaa-55d9-b0d0-60b623202d97.name: British Government inquires into the finances of Egypt
d017cc8e-acaa-55d9-b0d0-60b623202d97.description: In December 1875 Stephen Cave and John Stokes are sent by the British Government to inquire into the finances of Egypt. Their report, published in April 1876, advises that in view of the perceived “waste and extravagance” it is necessary for foreign powers to interfere to restore credit.

d079d874-cea1-54f4-aac5-e2753ec020fa.name: Symbolism
d079d874-cea1-54f4-aac5-e2753ec020fa.description: A reaction to Naturalism and Parnassism, Symbolism focuses on the imagination and spirituality. Inspired by Charles Baudelaire, the aesthetic developed (i.e. Verlaine, Rimbaud and Mallarmé) and triumphed at the theatre, in music and in the fine arts.

d09c6663-d561-54e2-990c-7f950c4e0c9f.name: Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey
d09c6663-d561-54e2-990c-7f950c4e0c9f.description: 29 October: Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey. Mustafa Kemal Atatürk becomes the first president of Turkey.

d09c9c7e-50d3-5a64-8d07-c6e9039df93d.name: Barcelona Universal Exhibition
d09c9c7e-50d3-5a64-8d07-c6e9039df93d.description: The Barcelona Universal Exhibition held in the Parc de la Ciutadella from April to December attracts exhibitors from 22 countries and more than two million visitors. The park displays monuments in the Modernismo/Modernisme and Neo-Mudéjar styles.

d0a9135d-4760-5f28-9200-b4ad750e96a7.name: Gualberta Alaide Beccari founds the periodical *La donna*
d0a9135d-4760-5f28-9200-b4ad750e96a7.description: Gualberta Alaide Beccari (a feminist with republican ideas, much influenced by Mazzini) founds the periodical *La donna*, which campaigns for women’s rights. *La donna*’s main contributor is Anna Maria Mozzoni, who since 1865 had campaigned against “marital authorisation” and for women’s right to vote.

d0ada20c-ed73-58a2-888b-fb8ac362aa21.name: Heinrich Schliemann in Troy
d0ada20c-ed73-58a2-888b-fb8ac362aa21.description: German archaeologist Heinrich Schliemann (1822–90) begins excavations in Troy.

d0d5cca8-455e-57b4-a64e-4df10dda0bf3.name: Second Serbian Uprising
d0d5cca8-455e-57b4-a64e-4df10dda0bf3.description: The Second Serbian Uprising – the Takovo Uprising – represents the second stage of the Serbian revolt against the Ottoman Empire, which breaks out soon after. The revolt leads to recognition of Serbian autonomy within the Ottoman Empire and establishment of the *Kneževina* (Principality) of Serbia, which obtained its own Assembly, Constitution and ruling dynasty.

d0e6f9ac-b95d-549b-acbb-6ed1774d43ba.name: In Turin, inauguration of the Royal Museum of Egyptian Antiquities
d0e6f9ac-b95d-549b-acbb-6ed1774d43ba.description: In Turin, inauguration of the Royal Museum of Egyptian Antiquities. The Museum holding includes 5,268 Egyptian items brought to Italy by Bernardino Drovetti and bought by the King of Sardinia, Charles Felix of Savoy.

d130127f-f82c-5213-acd3-42330b4787fa.name: The revolutionary General Josef Zachariasz Bem fled
d130127f-f82c-5213-acd3-42330b4787fa.description: The revolutionary General Józef Zachariasz Bem flees Austria for the Ottoman Empire along with 6,000 Hungarian soldiers. He becomes a Turkish General and in 1850 suppresses a Muslim pogrom against the Christian minority in Aleppo.

d24acba2-dc90-58c7-8d82-7ac4a6eaf1ed.name: Battle of Omdurman
d24acba2-dc90-58c7-8d82-7ac4a6eaf1ed.description: Sudan is in possession of the Egyptians until a Sudanese revolt under the Mahdi severs the connection. It is brought back to Anglo-Egyptian rule with a military conquest led by an Egyptian army officered by the British. Control of Sudan facilitated British colonial expansion in Sub-Saharan Africa.

d26bb3d4-3212-5037-9845-e2d4a9bff5c8.name: Al. Saabner-Tuduri publishes a book
d26bb3d4-3212-5037-9845-e2d4a9bff5c8.description: Al. Saabner-Tuduri publishes a book on the *Mineral Waters and the Spas of Romania*, the first paper about Romanian balneology, which used to be a very important component of Romanian tourism.

d2c0dfdc-0ee2-5a79-9858-a973cab46033.name: Publication of the first volume of *Study of the Life of Modern Greeks*
d2c0dfdc-0ee2-5a79-9858-a973cab46033.description: Nikolaos Politis publishes the first volume of his pioneering work on Greek folklore, *Study of the Life of Modern Greeks: Modern Greek Mythology*.

d2c2c7bf-c780-5ce2-a922-2d07c99a12b8.name: An industrial school for girls
d2c2c7bf-c780-5ce2-a922-2d07c99a12b8.description: 7 May: An industrial school for girls is opened in İstanbul.

d2cedb51-3e3d-5337-ac3f-a2adfe7f50ce.name: The German orientalist, archaeologist and investigator
d2cedb51-3e3d-5337-ac3f-a2adfe7f50ce.description: The international reputations of the Orientalist, archaeologist and investigator of inscriptions Ernst Herzfeld and art historian Friedrich Sarre were assured when they found 8,000-year old (6th-century) painted pottery known as Samarra-Ware. Some of these finds from Samarra are in the Museum of Islamic Art, Berlin.

d2ed96f0-bc95-5de2-8f63-94072e8c426f.name: International Exhibition in Milan
d2ed96f0-bc95-5de2-8f63-94072e8c426f.description: International Exhibition in Milan to celebrate the opening of the Simplon Tunnel. The main focus is on transport. There are 35,000 exhibitors, coming from dozens of different countries, and more than 5 million visitors.

d30e14d2-3626-59ea-aa45-7097c12df8d6.name: Founding of the Museo Nacional del Prado
d30e14d2-3626-59ea-aa45-7097c12df8d6.description: Founding of the Museo Nacional del Prado with the Royal collection of paintings as one the first museums in Spain.

d3295a15-ebca-529f-9fa9-465275939068.name: Opening of House of Arab Antiquities
d3295a15-ebca-529f-9fa9-465275939068.description: The House of Arab Antiquities opens on 28 December 1903, located on Bab al-Khalq Square which is famous for its Islamic infrastructure: the mosques of Ahmad ibn Tulun and Muhammad ‘Ali, and the Citadel of Saladin. The Museum is only the second concrete-iron building to be constructed after the Egyptian Museum.

d337e4c9-2216-5b7d-adbe-b71f477173f0.name: At the International Exposition held in Paris
d337e4c9-2216-5b7d-adbe-b71f477173f0.description: At the International Exposition held in Paris, the United Principalities of Wallachia and Moldavia have their own pavilions.

d36a2fb7-1f1a-55a1-9213-f7aeba3c7099.name: Adoption of a protectionist policy
d36a2fb7-1f1a-55a1-9213-f7aeba3c7099.description: Adoption of a protectionist policy aimed at boosting industrial development.

d390ee6b-f57a-5961-9447-5306a74d0e45.name: Zeppelin invents zeppelin
d390ee6b-f57a-5961-9447-5306a74d0e45.description: Ferdinand Graf von Zeppelin invents the zeppelin, a steerable airship.

d3f917c2-9d10-5df5-9edc-ddde543ede40.name: Bayt al-Suhaymi
d3f917c2-9d10-5df5-9edc-ddde543ede40.description: The residence, Bayt al-Suhaymi is built.

d4860780-9509-5d8d-b6f9-352b581af192.name: The Straits Convention
d4860780-9509-5d8d-b6f9-352b581af192.description: 13 July: The Straits Convention, signed by the Ottoman Empire and the great powers, prohibits foreign warships from entering the Bosphorus or the Dardanelles.

d4feed27-bc79-56f6-84d7-9eff1b1f35f7.name: The Fine Arts School becomes a five-year higher education school
d4feed27-bc79-56f6-84d7-9eff1b1f35f7.description: The School of the Fine Arts becomes a five-year higher education institution under its director, the architect Lissandros Kautantzoglou.

d510413b-29b8-5c3c-8250-2adf72dee3ee.name: Development of pilgrimages
d510413b-29b8-5c3c-8250-2adf72dee3ee.description: Development of pilgrimages in France, in particular to Lourdes, thanks to faster modes of transport such as rail.

d58c6de8-861f-5daf-b264-964fd2ab79e1.name: Issuing of the journal Autonomous Macedonia
d58c6de8-861f-5daf-b264-964fd2ab79e1.description: Publication of the journal *Autonomous Macedonia* begins in Belgrade. This attempt to propagate the idea of an independent state initiated by Grigorie Tashkovic ends after only a few issues.

d5c7b381-15c2-5fde-a2d9-7f2e48b98be7.name: Adolf Loos designed the house on the Michaelaplatz
d5c7b381-15c2-5fde-a2d9-7f2e48b98be7.description: When Adolf Loos designs the Michaelaplatz in Vienna for the textile company Goldman & Salatsch, unusually, there is no ornamentation around the windows.

d5ee18bf-fa6d-5978-a139-5ebdd84668d9.name: In consequence of the Prussian-Danish war
d5ee18bf-fa6d-5978-a139-5ebdd84668d9.description: As a consequence of the Prussian–Danish war, Denmark retracts its demand for Schleswig and Holstein.

d611927c-31ee-58e5-97a4-eccae1a9dac4.name: Abolition of the Salic law
d611927c-31ee-58e5-97a4-eccae1a9dac4.description: Fernando VII has no sons, only daughters, so abolishes under Pragmática Sanción, the Salic Law, introduced by the Spanish branch of the Bourbon dynasty, which forbids women to reign. After the death of Fernando VII in 1833, his eldest daughter becomes Queen of Spain as Isabel II.

d611cc18-5113-5dc1-8356-d2c4152c6a3d.name: Sailing frigate *Ertuğrul* sinks
d611cc18-5113-5dc1-8356-d2c4152c6a3d.description: 16 September: Sailing frigate *Ertuğrul* sinks while returning from a goodwill voyage to Japan off the coast of Oshima in a typhoon that kills all but 69 of its 609 crew.

d6241003-1e81-5ab6-89e5-bd022ba669a1.name: The Ottoman Bank, founded in this year
d6241003-1e81-5ab6-89e5-bd022ba669a1.description: The Ottoman Bank is founded in this year, registered in London, to channel overseas investment in the Ottoman Empire.

d63d9614-3dc4-5914-bca6-562df6c9cf5a.name: Defeat of the Greek army duting the Greek -Turkish war
d63d9614-3dc4-5914-bca6-562df6c9cf5a.description: Defeat of the Greek Army during the Greek–Turkish War.

d66b8953-ce9b-5856-8f43-034bb380c392.name: Art Nouveau
d66b8953-ce9b-5856-8f43-034bb380c392.description: In Aveiro, art nouveau buildings are associated with a local middle class looking for cultural and social status. Some are “*brasileiros*”, coming back from Brazil to their homeland, and investors in trade and industrial businesses, thus contributing to local economic development. The art nouveau of Aveiro is inspired by French patterns.

d66d20f8-5456-5b33-a129-f8a7dbaccb2d.name: From 1830 onwards many Spaniards emigrate to North Africa
d66d20f8-5456-5b33-a129-f8a7dbaccb2d.description: From 1830 onwards many Spaniards emigrate to North Africa (Morocco and Algeria), coinciding with the French occupation of Algiers and as a consequence of the economic crises in Spain. The emigrants are mostly from the Mediterranean regions such as Alicante, Almería and the Balearic Islands.

d672da97-5bdf-5b58-b76f-ca32f1766f47.name: Phone lines concession is signed
d672da97-5bdf-5b58-b76f-ca32f1766f47.description: The concession for telephone lines is signed and they are first installed in Lisbon and Porto. The first telephone list of Lisbon is published with 22 numbers located around 1.5 km from the telephone exchange. Public telephone cabins were installed and opened from 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. though always available to firemen, police and doctors.

d68f58a7-6d68-5d57-abc1-bca3573e75b4.name: The Angelus
d68f58a7-6d68-5d57-abc1-bca3573e75b4.description: *The Angelus*, by the Realist painter Jean-François Millet.

d6d22b87-4333-572c-9d32-824cfd38f3cb.name: Creation of the Emirate of Transjordan
d6d22b87-4333-572c-9d32-824cfd38f3cb.description: By August 1921 this British policy has been changed and it is decided to establish the Emirate of Transjordan under the leadership of Husayn ibn ’Ali’s son, Prince ‘Abdallah, who will become King of Jordan in 1946.

d73f16e5-f68b-5454-96e7-031fd3f2da52.name: Average annual Italian migration to selected countries
d73f16e5-f68b-5454-96e7-031fd3f2da52.description: Average annual Italian migration (temporary and permanent, to nearest 1,000): France 37,000; USA 24,000; Argentina 39,000; Brazil 22,000.

d75650f5-0324-59fe-9eba-3fa8b94b5c37.name: Several modernist painters
d75650f5-0324-59fe-9eba-3fa8b94b5c37.description: In the 1910s several modernist painters such as Eduardo Viana rejected the current teaching of academic naturalism, still deeply rooted in the national taste. Their focus was the cubism, futurism and Dada movements in Paris, but also the Orphism of French painters Sonia and Robert Delaunay, living in Portugal in 1915–16.

d76b2df2-b979-5e3e-9d54-a2db6211d2cd.name: Elite of Transjordan society
d76b2df2-b979-5e3e-9d54-a2db6211d2cd.description: Palestinian and Damascene merchants have long-established trade relations with Transjordan villages. There is a steady trade between al-Salt and Nablus, Karak and Hebron and between Ma’an and Gaza. Large families of these merchants move to these towns. They build many structures and become major landowners and form the elite of Transjordan society. These merchants become the dominant economic force and open up Transjordan to regional trade.

d7bce851-27eb-503f-8905-fde32112d088.name: The Ottoman Empire participates in the International Exhibition in Paris
d7bce851-27eb-503f-8905-fde32112d088.description: The Ottoman Empire participates in the International Exhibition in Paris. The Ottoman pavilions are designed in İstanbul by a self-taught French architect named Léon Parvillée in collaboration with the Italian architect Barborini. Sultan Abdülaziz travels to Paris at the invitation of Emperor Napoleon III to attend the opening of the World Exhibition.

d7ce88f4-b27b-5747-b942-890542145a8c.name: The Civil Medical School
d7ce88f4-b27b-5747-b942-890542145a8c.description: The Civil Medical School is opened.

d8178e1b-75fb-5950-86bb-9b794229a34b.name: Giuseppe Mazzini founds the Giovine Italia
d8178e1b-75fb-5950-86bb-9b794229a34b.description: Giuseppe Mazzini founds the republican movement for national unification, Giovine Italia (Young Italy).

d8364c0a-cad0-57b5-8fbd-60a1b306db12.name: The 19th century was the age of rediscovery
d8364c0a-cad0-57b5-8fbd-60a1b306db12.description: The 19th century is the age of rediscovery and of opening up the monuments and sites of the Ancient East to Western civilisation. Most ancient sites of Transjordan such as Petra, Jerash, Gadara (Umm Qays), Amra, Umm al-Rasas, Mushatta and many others are explored, documented and identified during the 19th century.

d850ed5d-bc74-5a3d-91f7-0f61cba141bb.name: Museum of ancient costumes
d850ed5d-bc74-5a3d-91f7-0f61cba141bb.description: A museum of ancient costumes (Elbise-i Atika) is opened in Hippodrome (İstanbul) where old costumes of Janissaries are exhibited on mannequins.

d86ea402-7376-5664-9baa-d78d92e50dad.name: Leopoldo Alinari
d86ea402-7376-5664-9baa-d78d92e50dad.description: Leopoldo Alinari, with his brothers Romualdo and Giuseppe, opens in Florence one of the first photography workshope – Fratelli Alinari.

d87eae89-d0c9-53c2-8bcb-afaabcaac6ec.name: Banyan (Hindu) merchants
d87eae89-d0c9-53c2-8bcb-afaabcaac6ec.description: Banyan (Hindu) merchants from British India increase their commercial, shipping and banking activities throughout the Trucial Coast, particularly within the pearling sector. Soon the Banyan becomes the main financiers, controlling all processes involving the preparation and pricing of pearls for export to Europe.

d8958d56-4ee4-5cc0-8f53-fcf12d937c3a.name: Exchange of population between Greece and Turkey
d8958d56-4ee4-5cc0-8f53-fcf12d937c3a.description: Exchange of population between Greece and Turkey.

d8a27055-ed7d-5aab-9b98-f78989ffdaab.name: Universal Exhibition of Paris
d8a27055-ed7d-5aab-9b98-f78989ffdaab.description: The Exposition universelle of 1889 in Paris is the tenth registered World Fair held from 6 May to 31 October. It commemorates the French Revolution on the occasion of its centenary. The Eiffel Tower is built for this Expo.

d8bb351d-decf-56fc-824c-191e0f0f9636.name: By the end of July 1916 the ports of Jiddah, Yanbu and Rabegh were in Arab hands
d8bb351d-decf-56fc-824c-191e0f0f9636.description: By the end of July 1916, the seaports of Jeddah, Yanbu and Rabigh are in Arab hands. This allows the British to increase their supply of arms and equipment to the Arab forces fighting in the Hijaz.

d8bc661d-63f4-503c-b48b-b0c51ee7ebf1.name: Macchiaioli
d8bc661d-63f4-503c-b48b-b0c51ee7ebf1.description: In opposition to academic painting, the Macchiaioli movement (Telemaco Signorini, Vincenzo Cabianca and Silvestro Lega) experiments with “spot painting”, based on the strong contrast between light and shadow.

d8ce7929-c81c-5ccd-8918-12e13af1166e.name: Disire for the orient
d8ce7929-c81c-5ccd-8918-12e13af1166e.description: "Disire for the orient" arises because of the breakovers around 1800, as the Enlightenment already had changed peoples life to a more rationalistic way of thinking and the scientification of the public. Also the sumless wars, especially the Napoleonic Wars, produced nostalgia and desire for the distance, the unknown, the paradise... Authors and philosophers from the era of romanticism bothered this topics (e.g. Friedrich Schlegel) and they tried to escape into something magical- the orient seemed to be a imaginary world.

d8ec1137-293c-5e40-83cc-3e2b2997d0eb.name: National Theater D
d8ec1137-293c-5e40-83cc-3e2b2997d0eb.description: National Theatre Dona Maria II opens its doors. Inspired by neoclassical style it was built (1842–46) over the ruins of the former Inquisition headquarters, the Palace of Estaús. The Portuguese royal family as well as the aristocracy and bourgeoisie attend theatre performances.

d93de60a-a047-5e77-9e53-0a9f55de94cb.name: Financial crisis
d93de60a-a047-5e77-9e53-0a9f55de94cb.description: Financial crisis during the last years of Queen Isabel II's government because of public investments in the construction of the railway.

d9431a0e-1d4d-51d0-b852-91f79fa6ac45.name: Urbanism in Morocco
d9431a0e-1d4d-51d0-b852-91f79fa6ac45.description: The planning and development of several cities in Morocco (Casablanca, Fez, Marrakech, Meknes and Rabat) are carried out by French architects.

d97e75d4-3308-5947-bca6-3d8b8f11da28.name: Founding of the Alpine Montan Gesellschaft
d97e75d4-3308-5947-bca6-3d8b8f11da28.description: The Osterreichische-Alpine Montan-Gesellschaft is founded to mine the rich iron resources of north-west Styria.

da44f4fb-01f2-5741-a780-db9a3f02b20a.name: Italian companies participate in many internationa exhibition
da44f4fb-01f2-5741-a780-db9a3f02b20a.description: In the 19th and 20th centuries, Italian companies participate in many international exhibition, such as the 1900 Paris World Fair.

da638fe6-2ee3-5cd1-8c74-e28162c61443.name: First Italian national laws on the protection of cultural heritage
da638fe6-2ee3-5cd1-8c74-e28162c61443.description: First Italian national laws on the protection of cultural heritage. The new laws establish the principle of inalienability of national heritage and create a state administration (with national and local branches) dedicated to caring for cultural heritage.

da68654a-a664-5a29-a1bc-45f3ad119476.name: Development of the Ruhrpott
da68654a-a664-5a29-a1bc-45f3ad119476.description: Development of the urban district known as the “Ruhrpott” from where, by around 1850, many factories operated (known particularly for coal mining). Due to rapid urbanisation and lack of housing several important cities expanded rapidly at this time, including Duisburg and Dortmund. The railway network reached the “Ruhrpott” in 1900.

da854941-603b-5f8f-9bf3-b83b901f2a08.name: Theodor Wiegand in Priene
da854941-603b-5f8f-9bf3-b83b901f2a08.description: German archaeologist Theodor Wiegand begins to excavate ancient Greek city of Priene. He would start to excavate in Miletos in 1896.

da9f2411-7c61-5ded-bc8d-bbddf1185af5.name: Third Republic
da9f2411-7c61-5ded-bc8d-bbddf1185af5.description: The Third Republic had a difficult start: the Treaty of Versailles with Prussia granting Alsace and Lorraine to the German Empire, and repression of the Commune. After a period known as the “Moral Order”, the Opportunist (1879–98) or Radical Republic (1898–1914) set up a large number of reforms in all areas, which include among others: a law on primary education (1881–2); a law on freedom of the press (1881); the restoration of the law on divorce (1884); a law allowing Trades Unions (1884); and a law on the separation of Church and State (1905).

dacb1478-50ad-5c0e-b582-9b17678827bc.name: Industrialisation
dacb1478-50ad-5c0e-b582-9b17678827bc.description: The pace of industrialisation picks up significantly: millions of tons of coal and iron are produced and production in the textile industry is enhanced by the Jacquard loom.

dacf159c-2279-5d0d-a08e-24357cd0d58f.name: Muatiânvua Expedition
dacf159c-2279-5d0d-a08e-24357cd0d58f.description: The Muatiânvua Expedition to Angolan’s Lunda territory led by Major Henrique de Carvalho provides exceptional scientific data on meteorology, zoology, ethnography and linguistics and photographic records. This second great expedition aims to counter the diversion of trade from Malanje to Zaire implemented by other colonial countries.

dadf5b04-96a2-5796-9260-76d77dfb897a.name: First International Art Exhibition of the City of Venice
dadf5b04-96a2-5796-9260-76d77dfb897a.description: Opening of the First International Art Exhibition of the City of Venice, known as the Venice Biennale. The exhibition – organised to bring the city out of isolation – meets with great public acclaim (224,000 visitors).

dae43552-d27c-513e-a1f2-1fb22760af3d.name: The inauguration of the first railway line (Buzău-Mărăşeşti)
dae43552-d27c-513e-a1f2-1fb22760af3d.description: The inauguration of the first railway line (Buzău–Mărăşeşti) designed and built by Romanian engineers.

daf0b5c4-f1a7-52be-bc46-73df269abaa1.name: The Recherche
daf0b5c4-f1a7-52be-bc46-73df269abaa1.description: Publication of Marcel Proust’s *Du côté de chez Swann*.

db26084b-b736-541a-b8d7-7fad3642adb6.name: Carl Humann in Pergamon
db26084b-b736-541a-b8d7-7fad3642adb6.description: German archaeologist Carl Humann (1839–96) begins excavating Pergamon. He would later conduct excavations in Zincirli (1888) and Magnesia (1892).

dbcf715a-63bc-5a86-bfcb-5bd51209aba3.name: Upper burgeoisie goes more and more on educational trips
dbcf715a-63bc-5a86-bfcb-5bd51209aba3.description: The wealthiest among the bourgeoisie begin to undertake more exploratory and scientific journeys to “discover” the rest of the world.

dbd7d6f0-6375-5341-a6c8-18435e8fe92e.name: The Commune Law is adopted
dbd7d6f0-6375-5341-a6c8-18435e8fe92e.description: 14 April: the Commune Law is adopted by which cities and towns become urban communes, led by a mayor and a council. All urban communes must have a fire department and a hospital.

dc31b47c-bc17-51dc-b050-6de177b8c526.name: Taha Husayn
dc31b47c-bc17-51dc-b050-6de177b8c526.description: Taha Husayn is appointed Professor of History at Fuad I University, where, through his own will and craving for knowledge, he becomes the leader of the Arab cultural renaissance.

dc37377f-afdf-5e16-81a3-45e06c8dff8d.name: Exposition Universelle des Produits de l
dc37377f-afdf-5e16-81a3-45e06c8dff8d.description: Portugal is present at “Exposition Universelle des Produits de l’Agriculture, de l’Industrie et des Beaux-Arts”, with 441 stands, exhibiting agricultural products and commodities. King Pedro V (1837–61) has a pivotal role in boosting the national presence.

dc494962-c4c6-5e7c-89ff-c743d6438445.name: First german railway section is established between Nürnberg and Fürth
dc494962-c4c6-5e7c-89ff-c743d6438445.description: The first section of railway is established between Nürnberg and Fürth (6 km); the building of the long-haul between Leipzig and Dresden is finished in 1838.

dcc0484a-2951-5487-88c8-97254fffd335.name: Tribunal de Contas
dcc0484a-2951-5487-88c8-97254fffd335.description: The Tribunal de Contas (Supreme Audit Institution), the independent financial control department, is separated from the financial administration. The public accounts are verified by the Tribunal de Contas and approved by Parliament.

dcd1924a-2f08-537d-84a8-8b09f74137cd.name: The Neandertal is being discovered and examined by Johann Carl Fuhlrott
dcd1924a-2f08-537d-84a8-8b09f74137cd.description: A Neanderthal is discovered and examined by Johann Carl Fuhlrott and Hermann Schaaffhausen. Rudolf Virchow, friends with the famous archaeologist Heinrich Schliemann, claims that the Neanderthal is not prehistoric man. He is wrong.

dcf1efa2-4b35-5b87-9fdb-d1cae39cfe2f.name: Mass migration of Czech speaking farmers to Vienna
dcf1efa2-4b35-5b87-9fdb-d1cae39cfe2f.description: During the second half of the 19th century the mass migration of Czech-speaking farmers to Vienna to work for Viennese industries finally amounts to half the Viennese population.

dcf2d925-6ca4-5e16-ad35-9cd422512d91.name: Excavations at Delos and Delphi
dcf2d925-6ca4-5e16-ad35-9cd422512d91.description: Excavations at Delos and Delphi by the French School of Athens.

dcf31f5f-ad19-5bc9-b9fa-a4171fcde7c8.name: The first Portuguese major code used almost a century was commissioned to António Luís Seabra
dcf31f5f-ad19-5bc9-b9fa-a4171fcde7c8.description: July: The first Portuguese major Civil Code is entrusted to António Luís Seabra (1798–1895), the first methodical code maker in Portugal. It is intended to meet the liberal need to regulate the juridical system as happened with French Napoleonic Code. One of its main concerns is the regulation of civil marriage. The Code will remain in force for nearly a century.

dcfc0230-ec3a-5f02-90af-9a076866ee79.name: Gray, Paul and Co, a British Company
dcfc0230-ec3a-5f02-90af-9a076866ee79.description: Gray, Paul and Co, a British Company, establishes a shipping office in Lingah, a city within Qawasim territory, located on the Persian littoral of the Arabian Gulf. The port first served for mail delivery and as a transshipment centre for traffic to and from Bahrain and the Trucial Coast. Later until 1902 all pearls from the Trucial Coast were exported to British India via this port.

dd337770-0c88-5c02-95de-16a1693a6bb6.name: Moorish or Alhambresque style
dd337770-0c88-5c02-95de-16a1693a6bb6.description: From the 1830s onwards the Moorish or Alhambresque style is popular in Europe, especially in Spain, but also in England, Austria, Russia, Germany and the USA. This style is found not only in applied arts but also in architecture and interior decoration including the well-known “Moorish” smoking or retiring rooms.

dd4b1947-f2cd-52eb-8d5d-31e1baebbbcd.name: First comprehensive law on health services
dd4b1947-f2cd-52eb-8d5d-31e1baebbbcd.description: First comprehensive law on health services.

dd6f5043-85e6-5172-aa2d-612e522398e8.name: Labour law
dd6f5043-85e6-5172-aa2d-612e522398e8.description: Law of 22 March 1841, inspired by the work of Louis-René Villermé: the Act prohibits the employment of children younger than eight years. It limits the working day to eight hours for ages 8–12 and twelve hours for ages 12–16. Night work (9 p.m.–5 a.m.) is prohibited for anyone under 13 years; and for those who are older two hours is to be paid as three.

dd959a6b-0f06-57a9-83ab-2d3e5f5d0acc.name: Tunis is a cosmopolitan city according to M. J. Henry Dunant
dd959a6b-0f06-57a9-83ab-2d3e5f5d0acc.description: Tunis is a cosmopolitan city. According to M. J. Henry Dunant, when visiting the regency in 1856, he noted that: “more than 15 Christian nations are represented by a number of their nationals in Tunis”.

dda502bf-d1f3-5915-8ae2-2e92a89849e1.name: Law on children's work
dda502bf-d1f3-5915-8ae2-2e92a89849e1.description: Legislation passed prohibiting children under the age of 9 from working in factories and mines and those under the age of 12 from working at night.

ddc71768-1a93-5722-a420-1fe63b2095b4.name: Great Depression. The Panic of 1857
ddc71768-1a93-5722-a420-1fe63b2095b4.description: The Great Depression, which starts in the United states with the panic of 1857, represents the first global economic crisis.

dde39fd7-51c0-501e-a6b1-b1daf7f6d3e3.name: The Numismatic Museum was established in 1834
dde39fd7-51c0-501e-a6b1-b1daf7f6d3e3.description: The Numismatic Museum is established. In 1843, it is amalgamated with the National Library and housed in a room at the University of Athens.

de2f000c-cfaa-5bfa-b2e4-3ec80a893998.name: The first Tunisian political party
de2f000c-cfaa-5bfa-b2e4-3ec80a893998.description: The first Tunisian political party is established as the Constitutional Liberal Party of Tunisia: “Le destour’’. In a pamphlet published anonymously in Paris, one of its founders, Abdelaziz al-Thalibi, specified the party’s demands.

de4beaa6-50e3-505f-9d1e-b5326eecf4da.name: Qasim Amin
de4beaa6-50e3-505f-9d1e-b5326eecf4da.description: Qasim Amin publishes his book *Les Egyptiens* in French in 1894. In it he rejects the negative claims against the traditions of Oriental society made by Duke Drocom in his book, *L’Egypte et les Egyptiens*. In defence of Islam, Amin compares the rights of women according to Islam with those of civilized European women. In 1899, he then publishes *The Emancipation of Women*, which is severely criticized. In 1900, Amin refutes the arguments of his critics with *The New Woman*, a work that provides fresh fuel to his ardent battle for the emancipation of women.

de76b8d9-e20d-59c9-8979-559cf1083e65.name: A paved road is built
de76b8d9-e20d-59c9-8979-559cf1083e65.description: A paved road, 6 meters wide, is built between Beirut and Damascus. It facilitates the circulation of the diligence (the transport company’s horse-drawn vehicles).

de8565a1-ea85-51ca-9f3e-c1bff5e6320a.name: Madrid Convention
de8565a1-ea85-51ca-9f3e-c1bff5e6320a.description: In November 1912 the Madrid Convention makes northern Morocco a Spanish protectorate.

deab9535-cb14-5536-93c7-8eede2460d3b.name: Fernando Pessoa
deab9535-cb14-5536-93c7-8eede2460d3b.description: Birth of Fernando Pessoa (d. 1935) is the classic author of Portuguese modernism. His books are published under different names, which he called heteronyms (not pseudonyms), each one corresponding to a cycle of experimental attitudes, which unfold in contradictions.

deb262b8-eae7-5330-a52e-db83f321553d.name: First World War
deb262b8-eae7-5330-a52e-db83f321553d.description: The duration of World War I.

deb8e4a2-d9dc-57af-b587-40484184dcad.name: Sultan Abdülmecid visits İzmit, Bursa, Gallipoli and the Aegean Islands
deb8e4a2-d9dc-57af-b587-40484184dcad.description: June–July: Sultan Abdülmecid visits İzmit, Bursa, Gallipoli and the Aegean Islands.

dec494c3-1b67-5083-9f8f-22fe01a9c778.name: USA declaration of war on the German Empire
dec494c3-1b67-5083-9f8f-22fe01a9c778.description: The United States declares war on the German Empire.

dec9b275-2e0f-5fd3-8fb7-300008cad022.name: Based on the Organic Regulations adopted in 1831
dec9b275-2e0f-5fd3-8fb7-300008cad022.description: Based on the Organic Regulations adopted in 1831, the National Assembly of Wallachia includes for the first time, apart from its traditional categories (the clergy and the aristocracy), representatives of the middle classes.

dece6950-3aa5-5170-9c0a-f3d976aabab9.name: Within Regeneration stable period mostly led by Minister Fontes Pereira de Melo
dece6950-3aa5-5170-9c0a-f3d976aabab9.description: Launch of an ambitious plan of modernisation and the stable Regeneration period mostly led by Minister Fontes Pereira de Melo (1819–87) (and named Fontism after him) Infrastructure building, industrial production and business laws are promoted. Porto wine production and trade thrives and exports increase until the 1860s.

ded926c2-f3e7-596b-bc2f-c6569f079b40.name: Bab-i Ali coup
ded926c2-f3e7-596b-bc2f-c6569f079b40.description: 23 January: Bab-ı Ali coup d'état in the empire (Turkish: Bâb-ı Âlî Baskını) results in Grand Vizier Kamil Paşa being driven from power and replacement of Minister of War Nazım Paşa by İsmail Enver. Effectively ending the London Peace Conference, it marks a significant point in the Ottoman government's progress towards centralisation, giving de facto power to the triumvirate known as the Three Pashas.

df341018-a7a7-527f-959d-d242ef197872.name: Champollion deciphers Egyptian hieroglyphs
df341018-a7a7-527f-959d-d242ef197872.description: Champollion deciphers Egyptian hieroglyphs, giving voice to the wealth of ancient inscriptions. This heralds the beginning of Egyptology.

dfc39f77-b0ff-5a65-8814-93ff388be630.name: Percentage of spouses who could not sign their marriage certificate because unable to write
dfc39f77-b0ff-5a65-8814-93ff388be630.description: Around 60 per cent of men and 80 per cent of women are unable to sign their marriage certificate because they are unable to write.

e021ab96-5d1d-5a33-8224-c58029550d82.name: The construction of the seaside resort Mamaia
e021ab96-5d1d-5a33-8224-c58029550d82.description: The construction of the seaside resort Mamaia, on the shore of the Black Sea, which became and remains one of the most popular Romanian resorts.

e06abb64-7056-51f0-a50d-c45916d72e15.name: At the Scala Theatre in Milan, premiere of *Excelsior*, mimic ballet by Luigi Manzotti
e06abb64-7056-51f0-a50d-c45916d72e15.description: At La Scala Theatre in Milan, premiere of *Excelsior*, mimic ballet by Luigi Manzotti, music by Romualdo Marenco. Through 11 allegorical scenes glorifying 19th-century scientific and industrial progress (steam-engine, electric light, telegraph, Suez Canal, Fréjus Rail Tunnel, etc.), it celebrates the triumph of Light over Obscurantism.

e12d03a2-2753-5e7d-9cf4-5df493da4b05.name: The Mandarin
e12d03a2-2753-5e7d-9cf4-5df493da4b05.description: Publication of the novella *O Mandarim* (*The Mandarin*) by Eça de Queirós (Queiroz) (1845–1900).

e14f45fc-6b3a-58ea-94d7-40fb369ef339.name: The Brother Luiz de Sousa
e14f45fc-6b3a-58ea-94d7-40fb369ef339.description: *Frei Luís de Sousa*, by Almeida Garrett. A romantic drama on the myth of King Sebastian, killed in the Battle of Alcacer Quibir, Morocco, in 1578. The myth of a disappeared king who will return to regain freedom and independence for his people underlies the plot together with the extreme love of Brother Luís de Sousa for his country.

e15c2ee9-9f86-5afb-af16-6900b2e91637.name: The Alaoui Museum
e15c2ee9-9f86-5afb-af16-6900b2e91637.description: The Alaoui Museum is founded in the bey’s palace in Bardo, in a wing of the complex formerly used to host the bey’s harem.

e178cbca-9129-58fc-9f03-73abb99febf6.name: The School for the Arts is established in Athens
e178cbca-9129-58fc-9f03-73abb99febf6.description: Athens School of the Fine Arts is established with three departments: the School of Crafts, School of Industrial Crafts and the School of Fine Arts.

e1c49131-797f-5c79-a5b7-5b72b88074e5.name: Heliopolis, Egypt, in this year, saw one of the first aviation exhibitions
e1c49131-797f-5c79-a5b7-5b72b88074e5.description: Heliopolis, Egypt, in this year, sees one of the first aviation exhibitions with an “Aviation Week”. While, initially, aviation was a sport, during World War I it became a weapon. It is only after the end of the war that aviation starts to be used as a form of “mass” transport for the wealthy.

e1faa967-9c63-5bad-b360-a10d88f3ce43.name: Les Meditations Poetiques
e1faa967-9c63-5bad-b360-a10d88f3ce43.description: *Les Méditations Poétiques* by the Romantic poet Alphonse de Lamartine.

e2142593-8a0c-522a-88f3-cd2fda090814.name: The railroad accross the Brenner Pass
e2142593-8a0c-522a-88f3-cd2fda090814.description: The railway across the Brenner Pass (via the Alps) opens.

e239639c-5018-5e36-93aa-584d4baf1696.name: Al-Manyal Palace Museum was set up
e239639c-5018-5e36-93aa-584d4baf1696.description: Prince Muhammad ‘Ali Tawfiq is responsible for opening the Al-Manyal Palace Museum in 1899, which is set in a large garden of thirty feddans (approx 31 acres).

e2a693dd-d5c5-5158-870a-fd111cd2e0a5.name: British support of Greek independence
e2a693dd-d5c5-5158-870a-fd111cd2e0a5.description: The poet Lord Byron epitomises Romantic support for Greek independence from the Ottoman Empire. Over the next century, British opinion wavers between seeing the Ottoman Empire as a force for stability or one oppressing Christian populations – the Armenians and Balkan Christians.

e325f5af-2955-5595-a935-0de8f642744f.name: The Jesuits build a modest school
e325f5af-2955-5595-a935-0de8f642744f.description: The Jesuits come to Beirut and build a modest school.

e32c717f-0a8c-5d81-b65a-79e555860a12.name: Italy is an agricultural country
e32c717f-0a8c-5d81-b65a-79e555860a12.description: Italy is an agricultural country. Political fragmentation is an obstacle to trade and economic development. The different states use not only different currencies, but also different systems of measurement.

e3483d0b-2cec-5de8-a557-470027b1771b.name: Architect Karl- Friedrich- Schinkel
e3483d0b-2cec-5de8-a557-470027b1771b.description: Architect Karl Friedrich Schinkel engraved a certain style on Berlin, starting with the Neue Wache (New Guardhouse, 1816–18) and followed by the Konzerthaus at Berlin’s Gandarmenmarkt (1818–21). Opposite the Lustgarten (Pleasure gardens) on what is now known as Museum Island in Berlin, Schinkel built the first royal museum, the Altes Museum (opened 1830), marking the beginning of the Island’s history.

e35ec658-4baa-55ac-ba19-050c4ade5fd2.name: The first Portuguese experimental psychology laboratory
e35ec658-4baa-55ac-ba19-050c4ade5fd2.description: The first Portuguese experimental psychology laboratory is created in the new Faculty of Humanities of the University of Coimbra by Professor Joaquim Augusto Alves dos Santos (1866–1924). The laboratory enabled the development of research on knowledge and memory and had a major impact on pedagogy and republican didactics.

e3616a2f-f0af-521c-90ca-c22e9c5c5ec1.name: The 1919 Revolution
e3616a2f-f0af-521c-90ca-c22e9c5c5ec1.description: The 1919 Egyptian Revolution is a milestone, not only in terms of the nationalist struggle, but also in the history of popular revolutions in general. Its overall influence, extending well beyond the politics and political parties of Egypt, exceeds the impact of the earlier ’Urabi Revolution.

e3a39cac-b22e-5660-b2df-510be7498dc8.name: Alfred Mitchell-Innes Under-Secretary of State for Finance in Egypt
e3a39cac-b22e-5660-b2df-510be7498dc8.description: British diplomat Alfred Mitchell-Innes is appointed Undersecretary of State for Finance in Egypt.

e3a9688d-05ef-5df2-ae69-f916aefdc9f9.name: The Congress of Vienna decides the restoration of pre-Napoleonic monarchies
e3a9688d-05ef-5df2-ae69-f916aefdc9f9.description: The Congress of Vienna decides the restoration of pre-Napoleonic monarchies: Kingdom of Sardinia (Piedmont, Genoa, Sardinia); Kingdom of Two Sicilies (Southern Italy and Sicily), the Papal States (part of Central Italy), Grand Duchy of Tuscany and other smaller states. Much of northern Italy (Milan, Venice, Trieste etc.) is under the Austrian empire.

e4b020eb-e1db-5203-bd29-56d67c4a279f.name: Freedom of commerce
e4b020eb-e1db-5203-bd29-56d67c4a279f.description: The intention of the trade treaty signed with France in August 1863 is to curb the damaging effects of protectionism and to limit the extent of European penetration but, subverted from its original purpose, it becomes one of the causes of the protectionism problem. The *Dahir* of June 1864 then proclaimed freedom of trade throughout the Sharifian Empire. The conventions of 1856, 1860–1 and 1863 established the legal bases for relations between Morocco and Europe. Europe’s influence then began to grow.

e4b102f7-1c36-5501-a631-79f377e163f3.name: Zoological Garden
e4b102f7-1c36-5501-a631-79f377e163f3.description: The Berlin Zoological Gardens was established in 1841 and opened to the public in 1844. The oldest zoo in Germany, today, it hosts more visitors than any zoo in Europe (around 3 million visitors per year).

e4e9a930-2562-54f3-8abc-b3540e05d1c8.name: British diplomat Alfred Mitchell-Innes appointed Under-Secretary of State for Finance in Egypt
e4e9a930-2562-54f3-8abc-b3540e05d1c8.description: British diplomat Alfred Mitchell-Innes was appointed Under-Secretary of State for Finance in Egypt.

e51306f9-7ebc-5fb3-a8bf-4084a48f8bf0.name: pre-March Revolution
e51306f9-7ebc-5fb3-a8bf-4084a48f8bf0.description: The Pre-March Revolution involves a series of protests, gatherings and disturbances, but by July 1849 the Bundes troops are victorious and the revolution fails.

e515f5f6-d284-59ae-89b3-f55b2a642322.name: Muhammad Sadiq Bey
e515f5f6-d284-59ae-89b3-f55b2a642322.description: Muhammad Sadiq Bey on a visit to Algiers is received by Napoleon III.

e54b2257-6fb9-5ba6-a775-47d338feaba8.name: Marcelino Sanz de Sautuola and his daughter discover the cave paintings of Altamira
e54b2257-6fb9-5ba6-a775-47d338feaba8.description: Marcelino Sanz de Sautuola and his daughter discover the cave paintings of Altamira. De Sautuola and Juan Vilanova y Piera in an 1880 publication identify them as Palaeolithic, meeting scepticism and ridicule until the discovery of similar paintings elsewhere results in recognition of their findings in 1902. Famous for drawings and polychrome paintings of animals and human hands the cave is now a national museum and World Heritage site.

e582ada5-0a13-5c75-993f-a679ea3bdad8.name: Uprisings in different parts of Italy for constitutional rule and national unification
e582ada5-0a13-5c75-993f-a679ea3bdad8.description: Uprisings in different parts of Italy demand constitutional rule and national unification. In Rome and Venice, short-lived republics are proclaimed. King Carlo Alberto (Kingdom of Sardinia) grants a constitution and wages war against the Austrian Empire, but he is defeated.

e5a1c209-06a7-551d-bc18-be366fcb9ccd.name: Crimean Tatars
e5a1c209-06a7-551d-bc18-be366fcb9ccd.description: The Crimean War causes an exodus of the Crimean Tatars, about 200,000 of whom move to the Ottoman Empire in continuing waves of immigration.

e5c0aa33-6344-5b2e-b4f5-8221bbde9116.name: Law about salary
e5c0aa33-6344-5b2e-b4f5-8221bbde9116.description: On 7 December the law is passed guaranteeing the payment of wages at regular intervals (every 15 days for workers, every month for employees).

e5f22dfc-b3c3-5502-9896-d4ae468e3089.name: Average annual Italian migration (1890-1899)
e5f22dfc-b3c3-5502-9896-d4ae468e3089.description: Average annual Italian migration (temporary and permanent, to nearest 1,000): France 26,000, USA 51,000; Argentina 37,000; Brazil 58,000.

e605c39b-dc49-5e6b-bbdd-0418b5fa191b.name: A primary school building to be built in wood called the attention of visitors of the Portuguese stand
e605c39b-dc49-5e6b-bbdd-0418b5fa191b.description: A primary school building to be built in wood attracts the attention of visitors to the Portuguese stand at the “Weltausstellung” (world exposition) in Vienna.

e62c068e-34a9-537e-82b3-ecb840f9139a.name: Romanian biologist and speologist
e62c068e-34a9-537e-82b3-ecb840f9139a.description: Romanian biologist and speleologist Emil Racoviță participates in the Belgian Antarctic Expedition, the first winter research expedition in the Antarctica region.

e63aeb47-1ac7-53bc-8730-89d528ec45ae.name: The Cent Jours
e63aeb47-1ac7-53bc-8730-89d528ec45ae.description: March–July, the *Cent Jours* (Hundred Days) between which Napoleon I returns to power and then finally abdicates after defeat at Waterloo.

e660aeef-0fc9-53fb-aaeb-4627b3096a8c.name: Panagiotis Kaloudis
e660aeef-0fc9-53fb-aaeb-4627b3096a8c.description: The “early conservator” Panagiotis Kaloudis works on the restoration of the *Chaironia Lion*.

e6630369-0acc-54a9-9f36-790e9cf4728f.name: Colonisation of the Germans
e6630369-0acc-54a9-9f36-790e9cf4728f.description: Germany’s colonisation of Namibia, Tanzania, Cameroon and Togo.

e68459a2-4c68-5b87-b966-ae7232ad654b.name: Peak of pearling industry
e68459a2-4c68-5b87-b966-ae7232ad654b.description: The period marks the peak of the pearling industry as the main export-commodity industry of the Gulf region.

e68564b0-bee0-50d6-9a4d-a76ce24c91d1.name: Kingdom of Sardinia, backed by France, wages war against Austrian Empire and annexes Milan
e68564b0-bee0-50d6-9a4d-a76ce24c91d1.description: The Kingdom of Sardinia, backed by France, wages war against the Austrian Empire and annexes Milan. Pro-unification insurrections in central Italy; Garibaldi leads an  expedition of 1,000 volunteers in Southern Italy. Italy is unified under King Victor Emanuel II (formerly King of Sardinia) as a constitutional monarchy.

e6d2aa53-98d4-5f8c-a7e3-143688535526.name: Urabi Revolution
e6d2aa53-98d4-5f8c-a7e3-143688535526.description: The ’Urabi Revolution, led by Colonel Ahmed ’Urabi, erupts in February 1879 and continues until 1882. It is the first revolution of the modern age in Egypt.

e75a9ecb-43ea-51aa-975a-024dd4811a5c.name: Petre Filipovski Garkata
e75a9ecb-43ea-51aa-975a-024dd4811a5c.description: Petre Filipovski Garkata and fellow artisans, including the master carver Makarie Frchkovski, create the iconostasis in the Church of Holy Salvation, Skopje. Petre Filipovski developed his own recognisable style of wood carving depicting scenes from the Old and New Testaments in which biblical figures were rendered wearing traditional costumes of Macedonia. The iconostasis also depicts the artists who created it as their “signature”.

e777e182-5099-5ee5-8e92-b66395fbbe63.name: General civil code
e777e182-5099-5ee5-8e92-b66395fbbe63.description: A commission under the chairmanship of Franz von Zeiller drafts the General Civil Code.

e7accde3-7983-52c5-aec3-f5daaae6ded3.name: The Romanian Philharmonic Society is founded
e7accde3-7983-52c5-aec3-f5daaae6ded3.description: 29 April: the Romanian Philharmonic Society is founded by conductor Eduard Wachmann with the aim of organising a permanent symphony orchestra. The inaugural concert takes place in the same year on 15 December.

e7ddb571-6ebb-51ae-a0a7-952796b9090d.name: Revolution in the Romanian space
e7ddb571-6ebb-51ae-a0a7-952796b9090d.description: Revolution in the Romanian countries: in Wallachia and Moldavia revolutionaries demand their countries’ right to self-determination, while in Transylvania Romanians want equal rights to those of the Hungarians and Germans.

e82f28e1-0c02-5755-ba4c-db905dbf39e8.name: The first Macedonian book History of the Frightening and Second Communion of Isus
e82f28e1-0c02-5755-ba4c-db905dbf39e8.description: The first book in Macedonian, *History of the Frightening and Second Communion of Jesus*, written by Joakim Krchovski (c.1750–1820) is published in Budim. Krchovski was a herald of the Macedonian cultural revival and went on to publish more books on religious matters. In the early 19th century in Macedonia only priests and other Christian dignitaries were educated enough to enlighten Macedonian people through literature in their mother tongue.

e86b7e94-46ed-53ef-a3ac-d1cba55b1cf2.name: End of first Saudi State
e86b7e94-46ed-53ef-a3ac-d1cba55b1cf2.description: The third Imam, Saud ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, faces a hostile reaction from the Ottoman Empire through its powerful viceroy in Egypt Muhammad ‘Ali Pasha. After ‘Abd al-‘Aziz’s death in 1814, his son, Abdallah, battles with the Egyptian army in many regions of the state. Finally Dir‘iyya is surrendered, and Imam Abdallah is then taken to Turkey, where he is executed.

e886172a-c9ef-514a-80fa-6ea01bb38850.name: Chinese migration
e886172a-c9ef-514a-80fa-6ea01bb38850.description: First Chinese immigration wave to France: 35,000 Chinese workers are recruited to France during World War I.

e88b2843-458c-5d46-82bc-255c520e1ace.name: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels publish the Communist Manifesto
e88b2843-458c-5d46-82bc-255c520e1ace.description: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels publish the *Communist Manifesto*.

e8a6828f-ee8c-573c-9acf-740dc8e4de6d.name: Redevelopment plan in Naples after cholera epidemic
e8a6828f-ee8c-573c-9acf-740dc8e4de6d.description: After the 1884–85 cholera epidemic hits Naples (the fourth cholera epidemic hitting the city since 1835), the government starts a redevelopment plan to clear Naples of slums and improve its sewerage and water systems. Similar renewal plans will be extended to other cities.

e8b37923-9ecb-5dc8-bf08-65b616aba2a8.name: The Qawasim and other Shaikhdoms
e8b37923-9ecb-5dc8-bf08-65b616aba2a8.description: The Qawasim and other sheikhdoms of the Arab littoral are held by Britain to sign a Treaty pledging to abstain from any interference with British Gulf Telegraph installations and to punish any aggressions made against them.

e8d8e9c8-0b8c-505f-9f0e-9f8cd8dbab43.name: Treaty of Kutahya
e8d8e9c8-0b8c-505f-9f0e-9f8cd8dbab43.description: 8 April: Treaty of Kütahya with Egypt. The Ottomans recognise Syria, Palestine and Lebanon as within the sphere of the Egyptian control.

e95ae377-30ed-532f-8c01-3c8616325978.name: Travellers and explorers
e95ae377-30ed-532f-8c01-3c8616325978.description: Travellers and explorers of modern times have scoured and described the Regency of Tunis. Their missions to the region provided occasions to discover the remains of antiquity and open up new fields of research to European scholars.

e9837c3b-9888-5fc7-8516-94341451d10f.name: The collection of Macedonian poems compiled by the Miladinov brothers
e9837c3b-9888-5fc7-8516-94341451d10f.description: Collection of Macedonian poems compiled by the Miladinov brothers is published in Zagreb. Konstantin Miladinov (1830–62), a prominent Macedonian poet, folklorist and educator is a major contributor. Despite a reference to Bulgarian songs in the title, the folk literature recorded by the Miladinovs originated mostly from the areas of Struga, Ohrid, Prilep, Kukush and Bitola.

e9acdfb4-fa2b-5954-8588-5aad2a2cfd48.name: Incorporation of the Ionian Islands to Greece
e9acdfb4-fa2b-5954-8588-5aad2a2cfd48.description: The Ionian islands are incorporated within the newly established Greek State.

e9c17608-c739-5869-90cc-702b8172cf50.name: Public health
e9c17608-c739-5869-90cc-702b8172cf50.description: “Medicine is a social science, and politics is nothing more than medicine on a large scale”, Rudolf Virchow stated in defence of public health and the building of hospitals in Berlin (i.e. Friedrichshain (1874), Moabit (1875, now closed) and Am Urban (1890); even parks and playgrounds were important to improve city life for the proletariat, Virchow continued.

ea1a6ee5-db2b-568b-a8d4-86e3aa084dec.name: Impression, Sunrise
ea1a6ee5-db2b-568b-a8d4-86e3aa084dec.description: *Impression, Sunrise* by the Impressionist painter Claude Monet.

ea1c0f9d-e983-5caa-a55d-83d0198230f2.name: Migration of Polish nobles and intellectuals
ea1c0f9d-e983-5caa-a55d-83d0198230f2.description: Polish intellectuals arrive in Paris, which becomes the capital of exiled Poland.

ea24c497-2776-5cf0-b000-3c4fdc1ed4f7.name: The second railway in Lebanon
ea24c497-2776-5cf0-b000-3c4fdc1ed4f7.description: The second railway in Lebanon is opened connecting with the first line at Riyaq and running to Aleppo, connecting it with Beirut.

ea4f6ecc-ca59-518c-a6d9-0ee1d626d297.name: The Madoz law introduced
ea4f6ecc-ca59-518c-a6d9-0ee1d626d297.description: The Madoz law introduced in 1855 provides for the state confiscation and sale of the rest of the Church properties and also of municipal properties.

ea57ecb7-7be2-5045-8bcd-423d006ffd16.name: The School of Pasha Street
ea57ecb7-7be2-5045-8bcd-423d006ffd16.description: The School of Pasha Street, the first school for Muslim girls, opens in Tunis.

ea76b19d-d318-510e-b037-2c49fe133c7e.name: Union of Moldavia and Wallachia
ea76b19d-d318-510e-b037-2c49fe133c7e.description: Union of Moldavia and Wallachia. In January 1859 Alexandru Ioan Cuza is elected ruler of both Moldavia and Wallachia, the double election being recognised by the Great Powers and the Ottoman Empire. In November 1861 the sultan issues a ferman approving the political and administrative union of Moldavia and Wallachia during Cuza’s reign. The United Principalities could now have a single government and parliament.

ea87b2c1-8129-5bba-8eb7-d10f77f6bdcc.name: Said Pasha and creation of Suez Canal
ea87b2c1-8129-5bba-8eb7-d10f77f6bdcc.description: Sa‘id Pasha’s accession to the Viceroyalty of Egypt provides French businessman Ferdinand de Lesseps new impulse to develop the Suez Canal.

ead46ac6-3164-578c-b1b1-c4b256d1befb.name: Invention and improvements to the rotary printing press
ead46ac6-3164-578c-b1b1-c4b256d1befb.description: Invention of and improvements to the rotary printing press allows for mass production of newspapers and books. The public are eager to read about the latest archaeological discoveries.

eb068311-0790-5a65-a15f-7a7ca3ddf767.name: Sibilla Aleramo publishes *Una donna*
eb068311-0790-5a65-a15f-7a7ca3ddf767.description: Sibilla Aleramo (pseudonym of Rina Faccio, 1876–1960) publishes *Una donna* (*A woman*), a fictionalised memoir that describes a woman’s desperate struggle to assert her individuality in a male-dominated society. The book is considered a feminist manifesto.

eb20588f-ef22-58ef-bf1b-79c990b32133.name: Max Weber is originator of the social science
eb20588f-ef22-58ef-bf1b-79c990b32133.description: Publication of Max Weber’s *The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism*. Weber is known as the originator of social science.

eb78e52c-1a04-55f3-8bfd-9c8b44dc2542.name: Capture of Algiers
eb78e52c-1a04-55f3-8bfd-9c8b44dc2542.description: With the capture of Algiers, France ousts the Ottoman Empire and asserts its claim to the western Mediterranean. The beys and the regency’s elite then become aware of the dangers posed by the Europeans.

eba9d236-769d-5999-8b5e-55ecab021362.name: Palace of Schwetzingen
eba9d236-769d-5999-8b5e-55ecab021362.description: The newly built Palace of Schwetzingen (built on the site of a former palace that actually dates back to 1350) flourishes under the Palatine Prince Elector Karl Theodor. Today a heritage site of great cultural significance, it contains some 100 sculptures and is known for its Türkischer Garten, a garden in the Turkish style with a mosque (constructed 1779–91 and the earliest mosque-style and largest structure of its kind in any German garden), designed by French architect Nicolas de Pigage and with “Oriental” details that are for decorative purposes only.

ebaf3d20-b569-5c17-901d-66c26b5cdce8.name: Bosnia crisis
ebaf3d20-b569-5c17-901d-66c26b5cdce8.description: Austria-Hungary annexes the Ottoman provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Following international protests, Germany shows solidarity with Austria.

ebb6b9d1-db65-5567-9e48-57eff6e6f6e8.name: First World´s Fair opened by Prince Albert in London
ebb6b9d1-db65-5567-9e48-57eff6e6f6e8.description: The First World Fair is opened by Prince Albert in London.

ebbd4b4c-6842-566a-967d-87f6a5507112.name: Pablo Iglesias founds the Partido Socialista Obrero Español
ebbd4b4c-6842-566a-967d-87f6a5507112.description: Pablo Iglesias founds the Partido Socialista Obrero Español (PSOE – Spanish Socialist Party) in 1879; under his leadership the socialists institute the Unión General de Trabajadores (UGT – General Workers' Union) in 1888, with liberals in power. At the same time the anarchist movement creates associations that later will become trade unions.

ebbd957d-2247-5a2c-a0ca-239a804b4a25.name: Colonial rivalries: the Moroccan crisis
ebbd957d-2247-5a2c-a0ca-239a804b4a25.description: Colonial rivalries: the Moroccan crisis brings about a new raft of trade agreements between the English and the French, with the participation of the Spanish, sharing out Morocco and Egypt, which is greeted with dismay by Moroccans.

ebc8c9b3-8450-557e-bc37-e0b3766b7b97.name: The Deutsche Volkstheater was opened
ebc8c9b3-8450-557e-bc37-e0b3766b7b97.description: The Deutsche Volkstheater (German People’s Theatre) opens in Vienna.

ebdb9af1-40e3-5a45-8333-cf5d7e62ae55.name: Weaponry
ebdb9af1-40e3-5a45-8333-cf5d7e62ae55.description: Weaponry is developed with lethal effect during the 19th century. The Civil War in the United States stimulates this expansion, but weapons of mass destruction – notably the Maxim gun – spread with European imperial ambitions. A huge disparity of power is created, shown by British military victories in Egypt (1882) and Sudan (1898).

ebec3768-0136-5994-a481-9c2f7bb12440.name: Gas-lighting is installed in the streets of Vienna
ebec3768-0136-5994-a481-9c2f7bb12440.description: Gas lighting is installed on the streets of Vienna.

ebfeed41-a5b2-5e36-819b-8c972b3aa95b.name: War
ebfeed41-a5b2-5e36-819b-8c972b3aa95b.description: War catches the people by surprise: British troops are fighting the Ottomans on three fronts. They are repelled at Gallipoli, pushed back in Southern Arabia, and British forces are captured in Iraq. By the end of the war these setbacks are reversed and Britain and her allies occupy Constantinople, Egypt, Iraq and the Levant.

ec2870c8-8f24-5991-935d-100a218348fb.name: League for the Promotion of Women’s Interests
ec2870c8-8f24-5991-935d-100a218348fb.description: Anna Maria Mozzoni and Paolina Schiff (an academic) found the League for the Promotion of Women’s Interests, the first feminist organisation in Italy.

ecacc515-a57d-5fc2-9102-2fd895ebb910.name: Direct rail connection Paris-Istanbul
ecacc515-a57d-5fc2-9102-2fd895ebb910.description: 12 August: Direct rail connection is established between Paris and İstanbul.

ed1587b0-9a1e-5ac6-b48e-8198dae5dee7.name: The first French-language newspaper Le Tunisien
ed1587b0-9a1e-5ac6-b48e-8198dae5dee7.description: The Young Tunisians found the first French-language newspaper *Le Tunisien*. Echoes of their militant action are seen in the riots of Djellaz on 11 November 2011 and the tramway accident on 8 February 1912.

ed342dc7-907c-5cf9-900b-f2c1a4bc0cfa.name: Issue of the first sanitation law in the United Principalities
ed342dc7-907c-5cf9-900b-f2c1a4bc0cfa.description: Issue of the first sanitation law in the United Principalities. The sanitation system is organised hierarchically and a Superior Medical Council, with a consultative role, is created.

ed9398cd-7bbd-55a8-8d39-00c64c1b5ccb.name: Coronation of King Carlos I on 10 October
ed9398cd-7bbd-55a8-8d39-00c64c1b5ccb.description: 10 October: Coronation of King Carlos I (28 September 1863 – 1 February 1908) Despite the King’s attempt to reform the political system, the growing urban influence of the Republican Party and the people´s discontent were fostered by cash payments made to the Royal House.

ee2795f1-465f-5602-a096-579b2f6b87cb.name: Law of Public Education
ee2795f1-465f-5602-a096-579b2f6b87cb.description: The Ley de Instrucción Pública (Law of Public Education) establishes three stages of education: primary, secondary and university. Primary school is compulsory for all children (boys and girls) providing the basis for combatting illiteracy.

ee89b1b6-7a6e-562f-8a84-ac664f0a12f0.name: Lisbon Astronomical Observatory is the Portuguese national observatory
ee89b1b6-7a6e-562f-8a84-ac664f0a12f0.description: The opening of the Lisbon Astronomical Observatory, Portugal’s national observatory, which has legal responsibility for national timekeeping. It is located in the Tapada da Ajuda, a green area in the west of Lisbon.

eeb771a8-d41b-537c-ae62-afd308af891b.name: German migration to France
eeb771a8-d41b-537c-ae62-afd308af891b.description: The first German immigrants enter France.

eeb812c8-9767-5222-941a-e251ff8d3827.name: The pre-unification laws on the protection of cultural heritage
eeb812c8-9767-5222-941a-e251ff8d3827.description: The pre-unification laws on the protection of cultural heritage of the individual Italian states remain in force even after unification. Until 1902, different Italian regions are thus subject to different disciplines.

eeec2b67-906d-51a3-8254-dd743dc84915.name: Religious Orders are abolished and expropriated by decree
eeec2b67-906d-51a3-8254-dd743dc84915.description: May: Religious orders are abolished and expropriated by decree; some of the assets of the crown, the Queen’s household and the absolutist aristocracy are nationalised. Monasteries are closed immediately and their buildings adapted, but women's convents remain open until the departure or death of the last nun.

eeedff22-17cf-51ae-9d41-01604b40664f.name: Edification of Sharif Pasha Palace
eeedff22-17cf-51ae-9d41-01604b40664f.description: Muhammad Sharif Pasha builds the Sharif Pasha Palace situated on Kirdassi Street, off Hasan al-Akbar Street, in Cairo. The Pasha held a number of important posts during the reigns of Muhammad ‘Ali and his successors.

ef14891d-be44-5f11-8de7-75fbfc1f7fe8.name: Industrialization begins
ef14891d-be44-5f11-8de7-75fbfc1f7fe8.description: Industrialisation begins at a slower pace compared with other Western European countries. It concentrates in Northern Italy (Piedmont, Lombardy) and in the Kingdom of Two Sicilies. Silk production is the strongest industrial sector.

ef2ebfed-06be-5790-887c-90f9f186d001.name: The Tétouan war
ef2ebfed-06be-5790-887c-90f9f186d001.description: The Tétouan war of 6 February 1860: the Spanish, seeking to extend the borders of Ceuta and Melilla, exploit a raid by a neighbouring tribe against a redoubt built outside the walls of Ceuta to launch a major military action and occupy Tétouan. To end the occupation of Tétouan, the Moroccan state was obliged to pay a significant sum (20 million douros), which it was unable to do. As a result, it was forced to seek a foreign loan that it was able to pay back using customs revenues.

efa4cf1b-63dd-5c30-9b9c-905816f0c994.name: Carolina Beatriz Angelo
efa4cf1b-63dd-5c30-9b9c-905816f0c994.description: 28 May: Carolina Beatriz Angelo (1878–1911), a gynaecologist, succeeds in voting in the 1911 elections. Challenged at the poll because she is a woman and therefore ineligible to vote, she insists, replying that she is “a doctor, over 21 and head of a family” and therefore she fulfils all the conditions required to vote. The electoral law is revised soon after this event.

efc21828-9124-5e11-9771-508147e2ab25.name: Death of King Alfonso XII
efc21828-9124-5e11-9771-508147e2ab25.description: Death of King Alfonso XII. Alfonso XIII born posthumously. Pacto de El Pardo: agreement between liberals and conservatives to rule the country by turns. Regency of Queen María Cristina until 1902 when King Alfonso XIII comes of age.

efec963a-5aea-52ab-a72c-094cdb7eac97.name: Crimean War
efec963a-5aea-52ab-a72c-094cdb7eac97.description: Russia’s expansion to the Black Sea and the Caucasus encroach on, seize and annex Ottoman possessions. Britain and France support Ottoman resistance, targeting the Russian naval base in Crimea. Britain provides military and naval support to the Ottoman armed force.

f0375954-afa7-5bd3-9196-2aa11c9b365e.name: Death of Raphael Suares
f0375954-afa7-5bd3-9196-2aa11c9b365e.description: Trading had hardly started that day (30 April) at Shari‘ al-Borsa al-Jadida or New Bourse Street when it was announced that Raphael Suares, the leading *laissez-faire* banker-industrialist in Egypt, had passed away. The Bourse closed for the rest of the day. It was largely thanks to Saures’ efforts that Cairo had a bourse in the first place. His unexpected and early death meant that Suares missed by only a few months the imposition of the first ever bourse regulations.

f0378c93-047e-5f8a-bb0e-8b8246245a72.name: Austrians were defeated by a French and Sardinian Army
f0378c93-047e-5f8a-bb0e-8b8246245a72.description: Defeat of the Austrians by a French and Sardinian Army at the Battle of Solferino on 24 June sees terrible losses on both sides.

f03acc14-fab6-58ec-9a6a-fe9d91f669fe.name: Beginnings of Spanish Romanticism in the theatre
f03acc14-fab6-58ec-9a6a-fe9d91f669fe.description: The premiere of *Don Álvaro o la fuerza del sino* by the Duke of Rivas marks the beginnings of Spanish Romanticism in the theatre, especially tragedy, further developed in *Don Juan Tenorio* by José Zorrilla. All the Romantic plays have elements from poetry and novels and some have a historical background.

f057e27f-f00f-5bde-bff9-183740e0a3b1.name: Monetary reform
f057e27f-f00f-5bde-bff9-183740e0a3b1.description: Monetary reform. Ottomans accept bimetallism. *Lira*, *mecidiye* and *kuruş* become official units. 100 *kuruş* are equal to one Ottoman *lira*. Silver *mecidiye*s equal to 20 *kuruş* are issued.

f09fa1bf-bd44-53e8-8b1f-61e8de9ab1d1.name: Peace congress of Paris
f09fa1bf-bd44-53e8-8b1f-61e8de9ab1d1.description: At the Congress of Paris peace conference, Wallachia and Moldavia are put under the collective guarantee of the Great Powers (Austria, Russia, Prussia, Piedmont, the UK and France), while remaining under Ottoman sovereignty. The Russian protectorate over the Romanian countries is ended. Moldavia receives the southeast of Bessarabia.

f0b55954-ae02-5357-a746-03f780fa5f00.name: The first edition of the Living Artists Exhibition
f0b55954-ae02-5357-a746-03f780fa5f00.description: The first showing of the “Living Artists Exhibition” (for painters and sculptors), organised by painter Theodor Aman, takes place in Iaşi. The annual organisation of such an exhibition is established by a decree issued in December 1864.

f0d81456-6f03-5c35-a21b-03f8fa7d5e6e.name: Construction of Piazza Esedra in Rome
f0d81456-6f03-5c35-a21b-03f8fa7d5e6e.description: Construction of Piazza Esedra (now Piazza della Repubblica) in Rome, designed by Gaetano Koch. The newly built palaces with porticos around the square are opposite the Terme di Diocleziano (Baths of Diocletian) and connect the area of Termini railway station to via Nazionale, providing an attractive entrance to the city.

f1309d18-6fc3-5caa-98a7-114d441ea5ca.name: Weimar Republic
f1309d18-6fc3-5caa-98a7-114d441ea5ca.description: With the establishment of the Weimar Republic, the number of migrant workers declines rapidly.

f18a298c-0fdd-5841-8ed9-db5958e1c561.name: Code of craft guild regulations
f18a298c-0fdd-5841-8ed9-db5958e1c561.description: Enactment of a code for Craft Guild regulations offers workers some protection in the Austrian monarchy.

f192e3f9-0de4-5e39-aec3-6d7f669f1c58.name: Amadeo Sousa Cardoso
f192e3f9-0de4-5e39-aec3-6d7f669f1c58.description: February–March: Amadeo Sousa Cardoso, at the invitation of Walter Pach (1883–1958), exhibits eight works at the Armory Show (1st Show of European Art, USA) in New York, Chicago and Boston. The Chicago art collector Arthur J. Eddy acquires three paintings by Cardoso and promotes his work in his book *Cubists and Post-Impressionism* book, emphasising his colour techniques.

f1a40e8d-7918-5c5d-8d94-b3b038a3f855.name: The social democratic party was founded
f1a40e8d-7918-5c5d-8d94-b3b038a3f855.description: The Social Democratic Party is founded during the Hainfeld Congress.

f1bb7c10-1e6c-57ac-9b41-d27e7cb8f390.name: The first film in the Balkans
f1bb7c10-1e6c-57ac-9b41-d27e7cb8f390.description: The first film in the Balkans is shot by the Manaki brothers. Pioneers of Macedonian film, Janaki (1878–1945) and Milton (1880–1964) shot their first film only 10 years after the Lumiere Brothers. It shows their grandmother Despina spinning wool. Their first film of ethnographic value was shot soon after. It documents celebration of the feast of Sts Cyril and Methodius in front of the church devoted to these saints in Bitola.

f1e35d5a-0d4a-565b-9051-d9e0dafb3329.name: European and American Historical Exhibitions
f1e35d5a-0d4a-565b-9051-d9e0dafb3329.description: European and American Historical Exhibitions held in the Palacio de la Biblioteca y Museos Nacionales, Madrid, celebrating the fourth centennial of the discovery of America.

f21fae31-17b1-5548-8863-19d12673fb37.name: Wallachia and Moldavia participate in the Universal Exposition of Industry and Commerce, organized in London, at the Crystal Palace
f21fae31-17b1-5548-8863-19d12673fb37.description: Wallachia and Moldavia participate in the Great Exhibition of the Works of Industry of all Nations, organised at the Crystal Palace in London. Their products are exhibited in the Ottoman pavilion.

f2229af6-d7d2-5bfd-ada9-f83d41754062.name: Treasure in Troy
f2229af6-d7d2-5bfd-ada9-f83d41754062.description: Heinrich Schliemann finds what he calls “Priam’s Treasure” in Troy.

f24ce13f-ac08-5986-9202-833dd3c12280.name: Ottoman Refugee Code/Immigration Law
f24ce13f-ac08-5986-9202-833dd3c12280.description: Ottoman Refugee Code/Immigration Law is issued. Forced migrants-turned-settlers are given 70 *donums* (about 17 acres) to start farming.

f258c162-5afa-53dc-97a2-1a65f298faba.name: Austria declared war against Serbia
f258c162-5afa-53dc-97a2-1a65f298faba.description: Austria declares war on Serbia in July: she is supported by Russia, France and Britain. Turkey and Bulgaria enter the war on the side of the German–Austrian Alliance.

f2a72779-7feb-5a74-a2f5-dc6daf7807fb.name: The Arab Revolt
f2a72779-7feb-5a74-a2f5-dc6daf7807fb.description: The Arab Revolt begins on 10 June 1916 led by the Governor of Mecca (Makkah), Sharif Husayn ibn ‘Ali, and his sons, the amirs ‘Ali and Faisal. His forces seize the city of Riyad and force the small Ottoman garrison to seek refuge in the local fortress. Another of Husayn’s sons, Amir Abdallah, manages to surround and then take the town of Ta’if.

f2dbfd4a-2937-5639-9f38-c6e1fa8367c4.name: War and status of Mount Lebanon
f2dbfd4a-2937-5639-9f38-c6e1fa8367c4.description: The privileged position enjoyed by Lebanon is ended by the Ottomans in World War I: Lebanon’s semi-automous status is abolished and Mount Lebanon, an important territory at the international level, is put under martial law by the Ottomans. The Turkish commander Jamal Pasha occupies Lebanon militarily.

f2e0c66c-01f0-523e-923c-afad822bbbc9.name: Congregational and Presbyterian American missionaries
f2e0c66c-01f0-523e-923c-afad822bbbc9.description: Established by Congregational and Presbyterian American missionaries, the National Evangelical Church of Beirut is the oldest and largest of nine congregations situated outside Beirut.

f2e97bee-ecc2-5dd8-9315-3224384abab6.name: The Austrian republic is founded in Vienna
f2e97bee-ecc2-5dd8-9315-3224384abab6.description: Emperor Charles I renounces his participation to the government of Germany-Austria (Deutsch Österreich). The Austrian republic is founded in Vienna.

f2ea8421-d374-5b7a-8b01-218f5ed21b02.name: Transilvania integrated into the Hungarian kingdom
f2ea8421-d374-5b7a-8b01-218f5ed21b02.description: The centre of present-day Transylvania is integrated into the Hungarian kingdom after the creation of the Austro-Hungarian monarchy. Partium and Banat had already been included in Hungary.

f31ed942-398d-5e25-8ba1-fc80be2d3354.name: The 20th century is undoubtedly one of urbanisation
f31ed942-398d-5e25-8ba1-fc80be2d3354.description: The 20th century is undoubtedly one of urbanisation. Outside the Arab medina a new city develops to host the many Europeans who have arrived to promote development of the colonial economy.

f372a4a8-8356-59ed-bebc-aaf43afc846c.name: Tax system is reorganised
f372a4a8-8356-59ed-bebc-aaf43afc846c.description: 7 February: The tax system is reorganised.

f44c9645-723a-5045-86ba-4f19c1d7284a.name: Ottoman and Egyptian navy destroyed at Navarino
f44c9645-723a-5045-86ba-4f19c1d7284a.description: 20 October: A joint British, French and Russian fleet destroys the Ottoman and Egyptian navy at Navarino as the Sublime Porte did not accept the declaration of the UK, France and Russia for an autonomous Greece (in the Protocol of London, 6 July 1827).

f451bf74-4526-5a39-919b-99c4469b8150.name: The Paris Exhibition
f451bf74-4526-5a39-919b-99c4469b8150.description: The Paris Exhibition is the major international exhibition of the century. In the aftermath of the Crimean War (1854–56), when France, Britain and Turkey ally against Russia, there is a boost of friendship with and interest in the Ottoman Empire. The Sultan visits the Paris Exhibition and then continues to London where he was made a Knight of the Garter.

f4b77d34-a2c3-54ff-8f0f-5fb446e01cb3.name: Nazım Hikmet
f4b77d34-a2c3-54ff-8f0f-5fb446e01cb3.description: Nazım Hikmet Ran, famous Turkish poet, playwright and novelist, is born.

f4befab0-f871-5219-9401-a56727e84665.name: Khan Antun Bey
f4befab0-f871-5219-9401-a56727e84665.description: Antun Bey Najjar, a merchant who made his fortune in Constantinople, builds Khan Antun Bey in 1853. It becomes a great business centre and the building is used by many institutions such as Beirut’s foreign consulates, the Ottoman administration, postal services, merchants’ offices and Beirut’s first bank, Imperial Ottoman.

f4bf7f3b-170e-5449-a50f-5cdd1aefc95f.name: Treaty about pearling and sponge fishing
f4bf7f3b-170e-5449-a50f-5cdd1aefc95f.description: The Qawasim and other sheikhs of the Arab littoral sign a Treaty with the British that enjoins them to request permission from the British Resident in the Arabian Gulf prior to responding to foreign requests for pearling or sponge-fishing rights along the Trucial Coast.

f4d13f65-fdbf-5940-a8ec-3b946bff2ff9.name: Inauguration of the Egyptian Museum in Florence
f4d13f65-fdbf-5940-a8ec-3b946bff2ff9.description: Inauguration of the Egyptian Museum in Florence. The bulk of its holdings are the items collected by Ippolito Rossellini during the 1828–29 Franco-Tuscan expedition to Egypt, together with the Egyptian antiquities that the Medici family had collected during the 18th century.

f4e71710-0e2f-592c-b1ba-6e469da47e2e.name: Carved wooden iconostasis was createdi in the Monastery of St. John
f4e71710-0e2f-592c-b1ba-6e469da47e2e.description: A masterpiece of Byzantine sculpture, the iconostasis in the Monastery of St John at Bigor near Debar is created in this period by Petre Filipovski Garkata (d. 1854) and his group of craftsmen. Carved in walnut, the iconostasis depicts scenes from the Old and New Testaments and varied floral motifs. This Macedonian master of woodcarving and his associates also executed the iconostases in Lesnovo Monastery.

f50ce420-1300-5385-93b5-449db62b2adb.name: Development of the railway network
f50ce420-1300-5385-93b5-449db62b2adb.description: Development of the railway network connects the city of Tunis with its hinterland. The network serves the large cities by connecting them with the agricultural centres created by colonisation.

f51633b9-d8de-5098-8516-badfbf827e61.name: Uprisings in different parts of Italy in favour of national unification
f51633b9-d8de-5098-8516-badfbf827e61.description: In 1820–21 and 1830–31, uprisings in different parts of Italy in favour of national unification and constitutional rule. They meet harsh repression.

f5404b47-b636-5d9f-a705-92c7df0ba4c8.name: Werner von Siemens develops tram
f5404b47-b636-5d9f-a705-92c7df0ba4c8.description: Werner von Siemens develops the tram.

f5423b25-6796-58d4-9868-08143b3d0803.name: Merge of Banco de Lisboa and the investment company
f5423b25-6796-58d4-9868-08143b3d0803.description: Merger of Banco de Lisboa and the investment company Companhia Confiança Nacional (1844–46) creating Banco de Portugal, which by 1887 shares the right to issue banknotes with other institutions. By 1891, Banco de Portugal becomes the sole issuer of bank notes for the mainland, the Azores and Madeira.

f562c18f-4d48-50be-8456-fd2d224e24b7.name: The second Saudi state
f562c18f-4d48-50be-8456-fd2d224e24b7.description: Following the events of 1818, the Hijaz returns to Ottoman rule. Then in 1824 the Second Saudi State emerges, led by Imam Turki bin Abdullah, and with its capital now in Riyad following the destruction of Dir‘iyya. Imam Turki is then succeeded by the sons Imam Abdallah and ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Faisal. In ‘Abd al-Rahman’s reign, in 1891, the Second Saudi State falls into the hands of his enemy al-Rashid.
